title: Scaling Green Innovation Without Expanding the Bubble: How CSR Practices, Supply Chain Digitization, and Green Policies Shape Innovation Quality
summary: The rapid growth of green patent applications has raised concerns about a quantity–quality paradox in green innovation: rising patent application volumes do not necessarily translate into genuine technological progress or environmental value. Instead, they may create a green innovation bubble in which applications remain ungranted, consume organizational resources, and fail to generate technological value. While prior research has explored corporate social responsibility (CSR), digital transformation and environmental policies separately, few studies have incorporated them into a unified framework to investigate their joint impacts on green innovation. To address this gap, this study constructs an integrated analytical framework on three CSR dimensions (environmental investment, employee rest protection, and charitable donations) alongside supply chain digitization and institutional policy support. Drawing on stakeholder theory and the resource-based view. Using 11,288 firm-year observations from 1411 Chinese A-share-listed manufacturing firms during 2016–2023, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models and conduct robustness, propensity-score-matching, and heterogeneity analyses. Environmental investment and supply chain digitization increase green patent output but also widen the application–grant gap, whereas weak employee rest protection reduces innovation output and charitable donations are negatively associated with both outcomes. CSR interactions reveal conditional complementarity and resource competition. At the functional level, planning digitization raises output while reducing the imbalance, and production digitization also improves conversion quality. Ecological compensation and green finance jointly help redirect resources toward substantive innovation. The findings show that scaling green innovation requires coordinated environmental, human-capital, digital, and institutional resources rather than quantity-oriented expansion, providing an integrated sustainable environmental management pathway relevant to SDGs 8, 9, 12, and 13.

title: Pengaruh Green Financing, Environmental Disclosure, dan Kinerja Keuangan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Sektor Basic Materials yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2022-2024
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of green financing, environmental disclosure, and financial performance on firm value in Basic Materials sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2024 period. Firm value was measured using Tobin's Q, green financing was measured using Green Coin Rating (GCR), environmental disclosure was measured using the GRI Standards environmental disclosure index, and financial performance was measured using Return on Assets (ROA). This study employed a quantitative approach with secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and sustainability reports. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 28 companies with 63 observations after excluding 21 outlier observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 22. The results show that green financing has no significant effect on firm value (coefficient 0.076; significance 0.789). Environmental disclosure also has no significant effect on firm value (coefficient 0.417; significance 0.126). Financial performance proxied by ROA has no significant effect on firm value either (coefficient 0.859; significance 0.244). The Adjusted R Square value of 0.007 indicates that the three independent variables are only able to explain 0.7% of the variation in firm value, while the remaining 99.3% is explained by other factors outside the research model.

title: Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience Through Internet of Things Integration: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: This systematic review is based on a search of five bibliographic databases covering the period from 2019 to 2025, from which an explicit inclusion process selected 34 articles. The Internet of Things (IoT) enhances supply chain resilience by providing real-time operational visibility and, through its integration with artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain technology, and cloud computing, by reducing operational uncertainty. Several obstacles persist, such as limited interoperability, ineffective governance, and a skills gap, particularly in cybersecurity. Interest in supply chain research has grown in the literature over the past decade, but studies of resilience in emerging economies remain insufficient.

title: Identifying Key Factors and Drivers Affecting Sustainable Auditing Based on Sustainability Reporting
summary: The present study aimed to identify the key factors and strategic drivers affecting sustainable auditing within the framework of sustainability reporting. This applied research was conducted using a descriptive-survey methodology with a futures studies approach. The study employed a paradigmatic qualitative model as the foundation for hypothesis development and cause-and-effect analysis. Data were collected using a researcher-made questionnaire distributed through block random sampling among experts and specialists in auditing, accounting, and futures studies. The cross-impact analysis method (MICMAC) was applied to analyze the relationships among variables and identify influential and dependent components. An 8×8 matrix was completed by six experts who evaluated the degree of influence among variables using a four-point scale ranging from no impact to strong impact. The research process also incorporated Delphi rounds and scenario analysis to identify possible future states of sustainable auditing. The findings demonstrated that uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence were classified as linkage and risk variables with high influence and dependence, while technology emerged as the strongest influential variable in the system. Stakeholder pressure was identified as an autonomous variable, whereas institutional challenge, auditor role, and sustainability linkage were classified as dependent variables. MICMAC analysis revealed a matrix fill rate of 87.5%, indicating a highly interconnected system among the identified components. Strategic variables affecting the future of sustainable auditing included technology, uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence. Furthermore, four future scenarios were extracted: symbolic auditing, trust-regulating institution, reactive-minimal auditing, and predictive and strategic auditing. The results indicated that the future evolution of sustainable auditing depends significantly on technological advancement, regulatory maturity, professional competencies, stakeholder pressure, and the intelligent use of artificial intelligence and ESG-based analytical systems. The study concluded that sustainable auditing is evolving from a traditional compliance-oriented activity toward a future-oriented institutional mechanism for trust creation and strategic governance. The integration of technology, sustainability legitimacy, auditor independence, and uncertainty management plays a critical role in shaping the effectiveness of sustainable auditing systems. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive basis for policymakers, regulators, and professional auditing bodies to improve sustainability assurance practices and strengthen organizational accountability in response to environmental, social, and governance challenges.

title: Unraveling supply chain resilience – performance relationships: insights from a smallholder agri-food chain
summary: Purpose This study examines the relationship between supply chain resilience and financial performance in smallholder agricultural supply chains. It seeks to explore the impact of different resilience elements on financial outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected by a survey of 276 supply chain actors in the lotus supply chain in Central Vietnam. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted to ensure the reliability and validity of the constructs, while structural equation modeling was employed to test the hypotheses. Findings The study revealed complex relations between resilience elements and financial performance in the smallholder agri-food chain. Among the elements, operational flexibility, readiness for disruptions, response agility and lower supply chain density were positively associated with financial performance. In contrast, efficiency, reserve capacity, financial strengths, recovery and supply chain criticality failed to demonstrate significant relationships in the smallholder agri-food chain context. Research limitations/implications Findings are based on one supply chain in Vietnam that might limit the generalizability. Originality/value The study expands resilience research to smallholder agricultural supply chains, highlighting the importance of certain resilience elements in volatile agri-food industries.

title: Building Enterprise Supply Chain Resilience through Dynamic Capabilities: From Efficiency-First to Resilience-First
summary: The past five years of pandemic, geopolitical realignment and component shortages have exposed the structural fragility of efficiency-first supply chains and have raised supply chain resilience to the level of a strategic priority. The present study addresses that heterogeneity by re-reading the supply chain resilience literature through the dynamic capabilities lens. A structured narrative review was conducted, and fifteen representative studies were coded along the sensing, seizing and reconfiguring microfoundations and across six disruption types; reported standardised coefficients were extracted and synthesised descriptively. The results show that sensing research concentrates on multi-tier visibility, digital twins and predictive analytics, that seizing research centres on the redundancy-flexibility trade-off, and that reconfiguring research addresses regionalisation, reshoring and friend-shoring. The synthesised evidence indicates that seizing levers carry the largest reported effects on resilience and reconfiguring levers the smallest, and that conceptual coverage consistently exceeds empirical validation across all six themes examined. Research attention tracks the salience of recent events, leaving demand-side and financial disruptions under-examined. The study contributes an integrative capability map of a fragmented field and identifies the measurement of capability bundles as the principal research gap.

title: Dampak Kepemilikan Manajerial pada Manajemen Laba: Antara Sustainable Growth dan Growth Opportunity
summary: Managerial ownership represents an important corporate governance mechanism that may influence managerial incentives in financial reporting, particularly earnings management. This study examines the effect of managerial ownership on earnings management and evaluates the moderating roles of sustainability growth and growth opportunity in consumer non-cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. The sample comprises nine companies, yielding 45 firm-year observations selected through purposive sampling. Panel data regression was conducted using EViews 12, with model selection based on the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests, resulting in the Random Effect Model as the most appropriate specification. The findings indicate that managerial ownership has no significant effect on earnings management. Sustainability growth also fails to moderate the relationship between managerial ownership and earnings management, whereas growth opportunity significantly strengthens this relationship. The Adjusted R-squared value of −0.023241 indicates that the model provides very limited explanatory power, suggesting that managerial ownership and the moderating variables capture only a small proportion of the variation in earnings management. These findings indicate that managerial ownership alone may be insufficient to constrain earnings management, while growth opportunities can alter managerial incentives and intensify the relationship between ownership structure and reporting practices

title: Supply chain resilience integrating a permacrisis perspective: Multi-agent simulation and topological optimization of Tesla Giga Shanghai
summary: In the current era of “Permacrisis,” global supply chains are transitioning from facing occasional “Black Swan” events to enduring continuous stress tests from “Gray Rhino” risks (highly probable but often neglected threats). This paper integrates Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) theory with Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) to investigate the non-linear impact of network topology on supply chain resilience. First, by introducing triangular structures into single-chain networks, we reveal a “Redundancy Paradox”: while moderate redundancy significantly reduces the system damage ratio, excessive connectivity beyond a configuration-specific optimum (six triangular additions under the parameter setting used here) accelerates risk propagation and exacerbates instability. The existence of a U-shaped optimum is robust across parameter perturbations; its precise location is configuration-dependent. Second, taking the Tesla Shanghai Gigafactory during the 2022 Shanghai lockdown as an empirical case, we calibrate the model against the observed W-shaped (double-dip) monthly production trajectory, specifically reproducing the cascading effects of the “Aptiv wire harness crisis” through the short-board constraint of the model. The simulation results demonstrate that establishing a horizontal collaboration mechanism among homogeneous suppliers (evolving from a Star to a Mesh topology) is superior to simple connectivity increases. Under identical random shock seeds and R = 100 Monte Carlo replications, this optimization strategy reduces the time-to-80%-recovery (days required for total production value to regain 80% of its pre-shock steady-state level) by approximately 74% relative to the unoptimized star network, while the steady-state production value itself improves by a more modest ∼ 9 % — i.e. the dominant gain is in recovery speed rather than in long-run output. This study provides a theoretical basis for manufacturing enterprises to build “strategic redundancy” and survive in extreme environments.

title: Digital Transformation and Energy Poverty Alleviation: Heterogeneous Transmission of Sub Dimensions of Urban-Rural Integration
summary: Energy poverty has become a major issue that impedes social equity, exacerbates the wealth gap, and constrains China’s modernization process. The rapid development of the digital economy and urban–rural integration has provided new pathways to address this challenge. This study adopts urban–rural integration as its research perspective, utilizes panel data from various provinces in China spanning from 2013 to 2023, and employs a mediation and moderation effect model to systematically examine the impact of the digital economy on energy poverty, its underlying mechanisms, and its heterogeneous characteristics. The research findings indicate that the digital economy can significantly alleviate energy poverty. The mediation mechanism of urban–rural integration reveals that spatial integration and non-agricultural employment serve as the primary transmission channels through which the digital economy mitigates energy poverty, whereas industrial integration may instead exacerbate energy poverty by reducing energy consumption levels. Heterogeneity analysis demonstrates that the energy poverty alleviation effects of the digital economy are stronger in low-income provinces, provinces with high energy intensity, and resource-based provinces. This study contributes to scientifically clarifying the causal relationships among the digital economy, urban–rural integration, and energy poverty, thereby providing a reference framework for developing countries of similar types to address structural contradictions arising from urban–rural dual structures and energy poverty governance.

title: ECONOMIC MECHANISMS FOR DEVELOPING YOUTH ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This article examines the economic mechanisms for developing youth entrepreneurship in the digital economy. Particular attention is paid to access to finance, digital skills, e-commerce, innovative start-ups, and digital platforms. The study employs systems analysis, comparative analysis, scientific generalization, and an institutional approach. Drawing on international research and materials concerning Uzbekistan’s digital transformation, the article proposes an integrated economic mechanism to support youth entrepreneurship. The findings provide a conceptual basis for improving youth economic participation, creating jobs, promoting innovation, and strengthening the competitiveness of small businesses.

title: Digital Technology-Enabled Configurations for Sustainable Supply Chain Resilience: A Dynamic QCA Study of Chinese Manufacturing Firms
summary: Supply chain resilience (SCR) has become increasingly important for maintaining stable and sustainable manufacturing operations under growing environmental uncertainty. However, existing studies mainly focus on the net effects of individual factors, providing limited understanding of how digitalization interacts with technological, organizational, and environmental conditions in shaping resilience over time. Drawing on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, this study examines how configurations of digitalization, research and development (R&D) investment, return on assets, asset turnover, and industry concentration are associated with supply chain resilience in Chinese manufacturing firms. Using a balanced panel of 300 firm-year observations from 60 Chinese listed manufacturing firms during 2019–2023, this study applies dynamic qualitative comparative analysis (DQCA) to identify multiple configurations associated with high and non-high supply chain resilience. The results show that no single antecedent condition is necessary for high resilience. Five configurations are identified for high SCR and five for non-high SCR, indicating equifinality and configurational asymmetry. The high-SCR solutions include both R&D-centered and digitalization-centered pathways, whereas low digitalization appears in four of the five non-high-SCR configurations. The relative coverage of these pathways changes across 2019–2023, with one digitalization-centered configuration (G2) becoming more prominent in the later years. These findings provide longitudinal configurational evidence on how different combinations of technological, organizational, and environmental conditions are associated with resilience over time.

title: Tail Risk and Earnings Management: The Role of Gender Diversity and Environmental–Social Reporting in International Banking
summary: ABSTRACT We examine the impacts of earnings management on the tail risks of banks using a dataset of 3297 bank‐year observations across 157 publicly traded commercial banks from 12 countries, covering 2002–2022. Our findings suggest that banks engaging in earnings management activities exhibit higher tail risks. However, this relationship is moderated by two critical factors: board gender diversity and environmental–social (ES) reporting. Specifically, our analysis indicates that the elevated tail risks associated with higher levels of earnings management can be mitigated by stronger female representation on boards or through higher ES ratings. These insights provide important financial implications and policy guidelines for multiple stakeholders engaging with the international banking sector and ES seeking to strengthen governance framework structures while mitigating risk‐taking.

title: Building Community and Supply Chain Resilience Against El Niño and La Niña Disruptions in Malaysia: Insights from a Qualitative Study
summary: Climate variability associated with El Niño and La Niña continues to generate significant challenges for communities, infrastructure, transportation systems, and economic activities in Malaysia. While previous research has focused primarily on environmental impacts, limited attention has been given to public experiences and their implications for resilience planning. This study investigates how Malaysians experience the impacts of El Niño and La Niña and identifies strategies that may strengthen community and supply chain resilience. A qualitative research design was adopted, and thematic analysis was performed on responses collected from 102 participants. Four key themes emerged: health and well-being impacts, disruption to daily activities and workplace operations, economic and resource-related pressures, and shared responsibility for climate adaptation. Participants described experiences of extreme heat, flooding, water shortages, transportation disruptions, and increased household expenses. Respondents also recommended improvements in drainage infrastructure, flood management, climate-risk communication, emergency preparedness, and environmental sustainability initiatives. The findings suggest that resilience to climate-related disruptions requires coordinated actions involving government agencies, communities, businesses, and individuals. This study contributes to the climate adaptation and supply chain resilience literature by providing empirical evidence of how Malaysians experience and respond to El Niño and La Niña disruptions, an area that has received limited attention in existing ENSO-related research. It further extends understanding of the link between community-level climate experiences and broader supply chain resilience planning within the Malaysian context The study further highlights the importance of proactive planning to minimise disruptions to infrastructure, transportation systems, organisational operations, and supply chain activities. These findings offer practical implications for policymakers, infrastructure planners, and supply chain managers seeking to improve climate resilience in Malaysia.

title: Mandatory vs Voluntary Corporate Social Responsibility: A Comparative Analysis of Corporate Social Responsibility Practices in India and Sri Lanka
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has emerged as a vital aspect of modern corporate governance, emphasizing the accountability of businesses not only to shareholders but also to society at large. While CSR methods are extensively embraced worldwide, the regulatory approach to CSR varies greatly among countries. India has initiated a mandatory CSR framework under section 135 of the Companies Act of India (2013). This statutory obligation has created a structured approach compelling companies to actively contribute to social welfare, environmental sustainability and community development. In contrast, Sri Lanka continues to rely predominantly on voluntary CSR practices guided by soft law instruments such as the Corporate Governance Codes issued by the Colombo Stock Exchange and individual company policies. This study conducts a comparative analysis of the CSR frameworks in India and Sri Lanka focusing on the legal, regulatory and practical dimensions of mandatory versus voluntary CSR. This research examines how statutory obligations in India have influenced corporate behaviour and enhanced transparency and created measurable social impact while exploring the strengths and limitations of Sri Lanka’s voluntary CSR practices. The research identifies the gaps in Sri Lanka’s current CSR system, particularly in terms of enforcement, reporting standards and alignment with national development priorities. By analysing case studies, corporate reports and existing literature, this study aims to provide actionable insights and recommendations for Sri Lanka. It considers whether aspects of India’s mandatory CSR model can be adapted to strengthen Sri Lanka’s CSR framework, including potential statutory reforms, regulatory oversight and enhanced corporate accountability. This research contributes to the broader discourse on CSR by highlighting how legal mechanisms can shape corporate social engagement and societal outcomes. Ultimately, the study offers a policy-oriented perspective for enhancing CSR effectiveness in Sri Lanka.

title: Green Finance and Economic Growth: A Literature Review
summary: Green finance has emerged as a critical catalyst for driving economic innovation and facilitating the global transition toward carbon neutrality and sustainable economic development (Marín‐Rodríguez et al., 2024; Yadav & Chandiok, 2025). This literature review provides a systematic bibliometric analysis and qualitative meta-synthesis of scholarly work published between 2013 and 2023, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines to examine the causal links between green financial instruments to environmental and macroeconomic performance (Çıtak & Hoş, 2024; Olugbenga & Bali, 2026). The study categorizes existing research into three primary dimensions: the mechanism of green capital allocation, the efficacy of regulatory policy frameworks, and the differentiated regional impacts of financial innovation (Liu et al., 2025; Ma & Chen, 2025). Key findings highlight that while green credit and bonds effectively redirect capital toward climate-aligned projects, their success is heavily moderated by institutional quality and regulatory clarity (Ali et al., 2025). Furthermore, the integration of emerging technologies—such as artificial intelligence and block chain—is identified as a vital driver for enhancing transparency, risk assessment, and operational scalability within climate-finance ecosystems (Bagarti & Pahwa, 2025; Singh et al., 2025). Despite these advancements, significant barriers remain, including fragmented policy regulations, high transaction costs in emerging markets, and a persistent “instrument-impact paradox” caused by the lack of standardized environmental accounting metrics (Jamali & Voghouei, 2025; Raman et al., 2025). The review concludes that achieving a resilient global green finance architecture requires a shift toward interdisciplinary research, unified global reporting standards, and the active role of development banks in de-risking sustainable investments (Liu et al., 2025; Sheraz et al., 2021). Ultimately, these findings offer a policy-action roadmap to align financial incentives with long-term ecological sustainability and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (Majumdar et al., 2026; Olugbenga & Bali, 2026).

title: The Impact of Organizational Ethical Culture on the Quality of Sustainability Reporting with the Mediating Role of Environmental Governance
summary: This study was conducted with the aim of examining the impact of organizational ethical culture on the quality of sustainability reporting with the mediating role of environmental governance in companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange. Given the increasing demand for transparent and credible disclosure of sustainability information, understanding the organizational determinants affecting reporting quality is of considerable importance. The research design was quantitative and descriptive–analytical, and data were collected through standardized questionnaires and content analysis of sustainability reports from 112 active companies in 2024. Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4 and SPSS version 27. The findings indicated that organizational ethical culture has a positive and statistically significant relationship with the quality of sustainability reporting (β = 0.34). Furthermore, environmental governance not only has a direct positive effect on reporting quality (β = 0.41), but also plays a statistically significant mediating role in the relationship between ethical culture and sustainability reporting quality (indirect effect: β = 0.19). These results emphasize that enhancing the quality of sustainability reporting requires the integration of ethical orientations with formal governance structures. The findings contribute to the theoretical development of sustainability accounting and provide practical guidance for boards of directors, regulators, and organizations in emerging economies.

title: TECHNOLOGY ADAPTABILITY AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AMONG SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN UGANDA
summary: Digital transformation has become an important driver of business competitiveness, operational efficiency, innovation and sustainable enterprise development. For small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies such as Uganda, the capacity to adapt to emerging technologies is increasingly important for business survival and participation in the digital economy. However, despite the expansion of mobile telecommunications, digital financial services, electronic commerce and government-supported digitalisation initiatives, many Ugandan SMEs continue to experience difficulties in integrating digital technologies into their business operations. This integrative critical literature review examines the relationship between technology adaptability and digital transformation among SMEs in Uganda, focusing on technological readiness, organisational capabilities, managerial competencies, financial resources, institutional support and environmental influences. The review draws on established theoretical and empirical literature, including the Technology–Organisation– Environment framework, Technology Acceptance Model, Diffusion of Innovations theory, Dynamic Capabilities theory and Resource-Based View. It critically examines the extent to which these frameworks explain technology adoption and sustained digital transformation within resourceconstrained enterprise environments. The synthesis identifies interconnected barriers involving inadequate digital competencies, limited access to affordable financing, infrastructure constraints, cybersecurity concerns, organisational resistance and uneven access to digital markets. It further highlights opportunities associated with mobile money, cloud computing, digital marketing, electronic payment systems, enterprise management applications and emerging artificial intelligence technologies. The review argues that technology adaptability should be understood not simply as the willingness to adopt technological innovations but as a multidimensional organisational capability involving continuous learning, strategic flexibility, technological integration and institutional responsiveness. It concludes that successful digital transformation among Ugandan SMEs depends on the interaction of internal enterprise capabilities and supportive external conditions.

title: Exploring the effects of supply chain network in improving supply chain resilience
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate how social network ties influence supply chain resilience (SCR) through the mediating roles of key internal capabilities. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on social network theory and the dynamic capabilities (DC) framework, this study proposes a conceptual model and empirically test it. Findings The findings highlight the complementary roles of strong and weak ties in building resilient yet cost-competitive supply chains (SCs) in a post-COVID global environment. Research limitations/implications The research provides a novel relational perspective that explains the micro-foundations of resilience in global, multistage SCs. The findings enrich existing SCR literature by conceptually unpacking and empirically testing the mediating pathways through which social connections across SCs translate into resilience capabilities. Originality/value This research offers a novel relational perspective by bridging sociology and SC management, and extending the DC framework by demonstrating how interorganizational social ties serve as critical mechanisms for developing and deploying key internal capabilities.

title: Advancing SDG 12 and SDG 13 in a Developing Extractive Economy: Corporate Social Responsibility, Stakeholder Interest, and Supply Chain Resilience in Ghanaian Mining
summary: ABSTRACT The private sector's contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals in developing economies depends on how effectively firms convert their social and environmental commitments into development outcomes. This study examines that conversion in Ghanaian mining, a sector central to SDG 12 and SDG 13, where weak formal institutions constrain the translation of corporate social responsibility (CSR) into sustainable practice. Drawing on stakeholder, resilience, and institutional voids theories, we theorise and test a serial mediation model in which CSR advances sustainable mining through sequential governance: it first activates stakeholder interest (SI), which builds supply chain resilience (SCR), which in turn drives sustainable mining (SM). We analyse single‐source, cross‐sectional data from 458 respondents across 116 Ghanaian mining firms using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM), with an artificial neural network, importance–performance map analysis, and a Gaussian copula test as robustness checks. CSR exerts no significant direct effect on sustainable mining ( β = 0.089, n.s.); its total effect ( β = 0.383, p < 0.001) is transmitted entirely through the stakeholder and supply chain pathway (CSR → SI → SCR → SM; β = 0.047, p < 0.01). The findings show that the private sector's contribution to the SDGs in extractive economies depends less on the scale of CSR expenditure than on the stakeholder partnerships and value‐chain governance that convert it into development outcomes.

title: Spatial spillover effects of the digital economy on green innovation based on time varying networks
summary: Introduction The digital economy reshapes interregional connections beyond geographical proximity, with implications for green technology innovation. Methods Using 2014–2023 panel data for 30 Chinese provinces, this study constructs an asymmetric, time-varying digital-economic network based on a modified gravity model and applies social network analysis and a Spatial Durbin Model. Results The results show that the network exhibits a persistent core–periphery structure alongside changes in provincial positions. Under the baseline network specification, digital economy development is positively associated with local green technology innovation and has a significant negative indirect effect on network-connected provinces, consistent with resource-competition and siphon-related forces outweighing knowledge-diffusion forces in the cross-regional channel. This negative indirect effect remains significant under an alternative geographic matrix, although the negative total effect becomes insignificant, indicating that the overall effect is sensitive to the definition of spatial linkages. Conditional decomposition shows that the negative spillover deepened before 2019, moderated between 2019 and 2021, and remained stable thereafter. Discussion Provincial evidence suggests that stronger connectivity does not necessarily improve the relative innovation performance of late-developing regions, as its benefits depend on local absorptive capacity and resource-retention capabilities. These findings highlight the importance of combining interregional digital connectivity with local innovation-capacity building.

title: Key determinants of the growing importance of digitization and cybersecurity in economic processes and e-banking in recent years
summary: Objectives The article aims to identify and analyze key determinants of the growing importance of economic digitalization, e-banking, and cybersecurity. It also examines the relationships between ICT development, Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence, and the transformation of business models in enterprises and financial institutions. Material and methods The study employed critical literature analysis, comparative analysis of secondary data, and a systemic approach. Scientific publications, industry reports, and studies on digital transformation and cybersecurity were examined using an interdisciplinary perspective. Results The findings indicate that cloud technologies, mobile solutions, and AI systems are major drivers of digitalization and e-banking development. Accelerated digital transformation has strengthened e-commerce and electronic services while simultaneously increasing exposure to cyber threats and the need for advanced cybersecurity systems. Conclusions The growing role of digitalization and cybersecurity is structural and long-term in nature. The integration of technological innovations with comprehensive cyber risk management strategies is becoming essential for competitiveness, resilience, and sustainable development in the digital economy.

title: Cybersecurity in the Digital Era: Implications for Financial Reporting and Audit
summary: This article examines cybersecurity as an emerging risk in financial reporting and financial audit, within a context shaped by the accelerated digitalisation of accounting systems and the increasing frequency of cyber incidents. The research adopts an integrated approach, combining theoretical analysis, bibliometric analysis, and an empirical investigation based on data concerning cybersecurity incidents. The objective of this research is to highlight the ways in which the digitalisation of financial reporting enhances the efficiency and quality of information, while simultaneously generating vulnerabilities that may affect the integrity and reliability of financial statements. The bibliometric analysis, conducted on a sample of 1,534 articles indexed in Web of Science (2015–2025), shows the consolidation of cybersecurity as an interdisciplinary field situated at the intersection of technology, governance, and audit. The empirical component uses data provided by Audit Analytics for 994 listed US companies over the period 2004–2025. The results indicate a concentration of attacks in economically and technologically developed regions, with personal and financial information as the main targets, and unauthorised access as the dominant attack method. The study confirms that cyber risks influence audit risk assessment, prompting auditors to intensify and diversify procedures to ensure the quality of financial information.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in India: An Overview
summary: Abstract Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has emerged as an important mechanism for promoting social welfare and sustainable development in India. This paper provides an overview of the statutory framework governing CSR under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, including its applicability thresholds, expenditure requirements, committee structure, governance functions, reporting obligations, eligible activities under Schedule VII, and the treatment of unspent amounts. It also examines constitutional and ethical justifications for corporate responsibility, with particular reference to the right to life and a clean environment, the Polluter Pays Principle, and the relationship between business operations and stakeholder welfare. The paper highlights the role of CSR in supporting inclusive and sustainable development while noting the continuing importance of integrating environmental and social considerations into core business decisions.

title: Evaluating Digital Technologies’ Economic and Environmental Effects on Compliance, Governance, and Privacy in Sustainable Environmental Management
summary: The purpose of the study was to analyze new technologies impact on environment. The prospective benefits and challenges of new technologies on the use of technologies within environmental governance and compliance were uncovered in this study. Utilizing a convergence approach of qualitative and quantitative studies, the researchers sent out a survey to 9407 stakeholders within the environment, which included civil society, the private sector, and government. The study found out that the enforcement and reporting of compliance with environmental legislation would be greatly assisted by the streamlining of governance and compliance in the adoption of new technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT), The study also acknowledged the presence of other challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, expensive technologies, and poor technical capacity. The gaps and challenges on the governance of the environment, compliance, and sustainability would be solved by the introduced new technologies, which in turn would create a sustainable environment. This would lead to the development of Nigeria in an economically sustainable manner, while also providing overall environmental sustainability. The paper recommend that Nigeria's should increase her investment in the construction of training facilities within the administrative regulatory systems of new technological systems in environmental sustainability, collaborative Joint ventures should be encouraged so as to achieve economies and environmental sustainability.

title: Modernization of the Classification and Indicator System for an Organization’s Resource Potential in the Context of Economic Digitalization
summary: In the context of the digital transformation of the economy, the emergence of Industry 4.0 and 5.0 concepts, and the expansion of the range of digital assets that act as independent resources for an organization, the relevance of modernizing the classification and assessment framework for resource potential is placed among the priority tasks of management theory and practice. The aim of the article is to modernize the classification and system of indicators for an organization’s resource potential, considering the factors of economic digitalization in relation to the conditions of medium-tech industry. To achieve the purpose of the article and disclose its main provisions, the following general scientific methods of cognition were used in the research: the method of systematic and structural-logical analysis, classification and typologization, comparative analysis, as well as the provisions of the resource theory of the company, the theory of digital economy and the concepts of Industry 4.0 and 5.0. I will draw the following conclusions: a critical analysis of existing classifications of resource potential analysis revealed their systemic limitations, among which are: lack of accounting for digital assets (data, artificial intelligence algorithms), network and ecosystem resources, static classification schemes and weak management orientation; it is proved that digitalization generates new types of resources and transforms traditional groups (production, labor, financial, information); a modernized classification has been developed resource potential, including six groups, where each contains both traditional and digital components, and network resources are allocated to an independent class; a system of quantitative and qualitative indicators is proposed to assess the allocated resource groups. The proposed toolkit can be used by mediumtech enterprises to monitor the effectiveness of digital transformation, diagnose “breakpoints” in resource management, and justify investment decisions in the field of digital development.

title: Institutional Challenges and Digital Opportunities for Women Entrepreneurs
summary: Women Entrepreneurship is kind of a pillar that holds up global economic resilience, helps mix different kinds of jobs and somehow supports long-term social economic growth too. In today’s world Digital Transformation— driven by social commerce sites, cloud tools and new kinds of money tech— gives women founders fresh routes to get past older limits, mostly the ones that come from not having enough resources. Even so, there is still deep unfairness in the system. Biased ways of distributing funds, plus strict social rules keep slowing down the growth paths, and that part feels stubborn. This study builds a plan that looks at two sides, the help that comes from Digital Transformation, and the barriers that stay put. It zooms in on newer markets, for instance India. By using Institutional Theory and the 5Ms Framework, we can see how online shops, marketing efforts and FinTech money tools work like forces that lift Women Entrepreneurship. At the same time it checks why the digital gender gap stays around, why Capital Asymmetry keeps showing up in venture money decisions, and why work and home life clash for many women in daily reality. The study ends with evidence based policies that bring big economic players together with small businesses. The goal is to support the United Nations SDGs 5 and 8, and push Socio Economic Development so it can reach everyone.

title: The Impact of ESG Disclosure ESG Performance and ESG Risk on Audit Fees and Non Audit Fees in the South African Quasi Mandatory Regime
summary: Abstract This study examines impact of ESG disclosure, ESG performance, and ESG risk affect audit fees and non-audit fees in South Africa quasi-mandatory environment. Using panel data of Johannesburg Stock Exchange listed firms from 2006 to 2024, we employ OLS, fixed effects, and random effects estimation to analyse the relationships. We find that higher ESG disclosure is associated with higher audit fees, suggesting expanded audit scope, greater verification effort, and increased engagement complexity tied to more comprehensive ESG information. Conversely, ESG disclosure is negatively associated with non-audit fees, indicating that transparent reporting reduces reliance on external advisory and assurance services. Similarly, stronger ESG performance is associated with higher audit fees, consistent with auditors perceiving sustainability activities and disclosures as more complex to assess, but is negatively associated with non-audit fees. In addition, higher Sustainalytics ESG risk is associated with lower audit fees, implying that ESG-exposed firms strengthen internal controls and governance oversight. Conversely, ESG risk is positively associated with non-audit fees, as weak governance compliance increases demand for external advisory services. Firms should consider ESG factors when pricing advisory services fees, and academics should consider the regulatory environment when assessing ESG factors and auditing pricing.

title: ESG Funds Research: A Bibliometric and Thematic Analysis of Emerging Trends
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) funds have received increasing research attention in recent years, yet the extant literature appears fragmented, with few attempts to bring together the scholarly works and chart out intellectual progression and future research themes. This systematic review article attempts to fill this gap by providing a comprehensive overview of ESG fund research with respect to its evolution, intellectual roots, and emerging trends. A total of 322 publications indexed in Scopus were identified, of which 67 studies were eligible following PRISMA-informed screening via Bibliometrix (R). Citation analysis, co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, and thematic analysis were conducted to map out prolific authors, journals, countries, knowledge clusters, gaps, and future directions. Results show that research on ESG funds has progressed from initial discussions around ethics and corporate social responsibility (CSR) toward recent interest in sustainable finance, data-driven decision-making, investment performance considerations, and regulatory developments. The studies primarily draw upon literature from CSR, finance, and environmental sustainability. The United States, China, and India account for most of the publications, while African, South American, and Eastern European countries are rarely represented. ESG, mutual funds, and sustainability form the prevailing themes of interest, while machine learning, Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, greenwashing, and resilience through crises are identified as potential future directions. This article reviews the literature on ESG funds using PRISMA-guided bibliometric mapping techniques. The review synthesizes the literature on ESG funds found in finance, sustainability, business ethics, and accounting. It maps the field’s knowledge base, conceptual foundations, thematic trends, and future research avenues, and provides an integrated framework for future research on ESG funds.

These technologies contribute to increasing the adaptability of enterprises to dynamic market conditions while strengthening their competitive advantages in the digital economy. The paper analyzes current trends in the digital transformation of ICT enterprises and identifies the key economic effects resulting from the implementation of intelligent information systems. A conceptual model illustrating the impact of artificial intelligence technologies on enterprise profitability is proposed. The model is based on the optimization of business processes, risk management, demand forecasting, efficient resource allocation, and strategic decision support. The practical significance of the research lies in the possibility of applying the proposed approaches while developing digital transformation strategies aimed at improving the economic efficiency and profitability of enterprises in the information and communication technology sector.

title: Impact of Digital Transformation on the Sustainability Performance of SMEs: The Moderating Role of Government Digital Support
summary: This study examines the association between digital transformation and the sustainable performance of small and medium-sized enterprises by considering the mediating roles of green innovation capability and dynamic capabilities and the moderating role of government digital support. The study integrates organizational capabilities and institutional support into a unified mechanism for explaining how digitalization is associated with economic, environmental, and social performance outcomes in an emerging economy. A two-stage design was employed: a qualitative instrument-refinement phase with structured discussions involving 35 enterprise directors in Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai, followed by a cross-sectional quantitative survey. This Study distributed 800 online questionnaires to respondents involved in digital transformation activities and retained 751 usable responses. The conceptual model comprised five reflective constructs and ten hypotheses. The study results show that digital transformation has the strongest direct positive association with sustainable performance and is also positively associated with green innovation capability and dynamic capabilities. Green innovation capability partially mediates the relationships between digital transformation and sustainable performance and between dynamic capabilities and sustainable performance. By contrast, dynamic capabilities do not independently mediate the digital transformation-sustainable performance relationship. Government digital support is positively associated with sustainable performance and strengthens the positive relationship between green innovation capability and sustainable performance. Given the cross-sectional, single-informant design, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The results suggest that managers should align digital investments with green innovation objectives, while policymakers should design digital support programs that help enterprises translate technology adoption into scalable, sustainable business outcomes.

summary: The article investigates the methodological foundations for the formation of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development under conditions of increasing economic, social, environmental, institutional, and technological challenges. It is substantiated that ensuring sustainable development requires the transition from the fragmented application of individual management tools to the creation of an integrated economic mechanism capable of coordinating strategic objectives, management functions, resource provision, and expected development outcomes. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the methodological foundations for forming the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development and to develop its conceptual model. The research is based on the application of the systems, process, integrated, adaptive, and stakeholder approaches, as well as methods of scientific abstraction, analysis, synthesis, comparison, systematization, and conceptual modelling. The study clarifies the essence of the concept of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development, which is interpreted as an adaptive system of interconnected principles, functions, methods, instruments, management levers, and resources aimed at ensuring balanced economic, social, environmental, innovative, and institutional development of an enterprise. Unlike existing approaches, the proposed interpretation considers the economic mechanism as an open and dynamic management system capable of adapting to changes in the external environment while maintaining the balance between strategic development priorities and stakeholder interests. A conceptual model of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development has been developed. The model integrates methodological approaches, management subjects and objects, management functions, methods and instruments, resource provision, sustainable development components, performance assessment, and a feedback mechanism into a unified management system. Particular attention is paid to the interaction of economic, social, environmental, innovative, and institutional components, whose integration creates a synergistic effect and enhances enterprise resilience, competitiveness, and long-term development. The functional role of each component of the proposed economic mechanism has been systematized according to its purpose, implementation instruments, and expected results. It is proved that the effectiveness of the mechanism depends on the consistency of management decisions, the availability of adequate resource support, the application of modern management instruments, digital technologies, corporate social responsibility practices, ESG principles, and continuous monitoring of key performance indicators. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the development of a comprehensive conceptual approach to the formation of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development based on the integration of methodological approaches, management functions, resource provision, and performance evaluation into a single adaptive management model. The practical significance of the proposed approach consists in the possibility of its application by enterprises of various economic sectors for developing sustainable development strategies, improving corporate governance systems, increasing resource efficiency, strengthening competitiveness, and ensuring long-term sustainable development.

title: A Study on the Value Creation Pathways of Management Accounting in the Context of Digital Transformation: A Case Study of Midea Group
summary: Within the background of the digital economy, digital transformation has driven the accounting function to extend from traditional external financial disclosure to internal operational decision-making, making management accounting a pivotal tool for manufacturing enterprises to achieve value creation. The home appliance industry is highly competitive, with significant pressure on cost and inventory control; the effectiveness of digital management accounting practices directly impacts the operational quality of home appliance enterprises. This research selects Midea Group, a digital benchmark in the home appliance industry, for case analysis. With the theory of technology empowerment, drawing on core literature on digital management accounting and combining the TOE framework, this paper examines Midea Group’s implementation path for management accounting tools during its digital transformation, analyzes the effectiveness of these implementations and existing shortcomings, and proposes optimization recommendations based on these findings. Meanwhile, this paper aims to provide practical guidance for domestic manufacturing enterprises of a similar nature in implementing digital management accounting. It also contributes to the body of case study evidence on digital management accounting in the home appliance industry.

title: Identification and Validation of Components Affecting the Sustainability of the National Banking Network
summary: The present study was conducted with the aim of identifying and validating the components affecting the sustainability of the banking network, using both qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, a meta-synthesis approach was employed, and based on a systematic search of reputable scientific databases, 79 articles were identified. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 16 selected studies were analyzed. The findings of this phase indicated that in the economic and financial dimension, components such as operational efficiency and sustainable profitability, credit and liquidity risk management, capital adequacy and balance sheet structure, exposure to foreign exchange risk, and asset quality play a significant role in banking stability. In the institutional and corporate governance dimension, ownership structure, effective supervisory systems, and macroeconomic conditions were identified as key factors. In the technological dimension, components such as digital transformation, development of modern banking infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the use of artificial intelligence for risk management were found to be of particular importance. In the social dimension, banks’ social responsibility, transparency in communications, and enhancement of customer experience were identified as influential factors affecting public trust and social capital. In the quantitative phase, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was employed to validate the components extracted from the qualitative analysis. The results indicate that the sustainability of the banking network requires an integrated approach that simultaneously strengthens the economic, institutional, technological, and social dimensions.

title: Considerations Regarding the Reconfiguration of the Financial-Accounting Ecosystem in the Context of Modern Digital Technologies
summary: Recent digital transformations are redefining the way the financial-accounting ecosystem operates as a result of the integration of ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) systems and artificial intelligence in accounting, auditing and sustainability reporting processes. As a result of increasing transparency requirements, the adoption of European standards on sustainability reporting and the rapid development of the digital economy, organizations have had to intervene in the process of conducting business, by rethinking operational models and governance mechanisms. The article aims to analyze how the use of ERP systems and artificial intelligence can contribute to the reconfiguration of the financial-accounting ecosystem, facilitating augmented accounting, intelligent auditing and integrated reporting oriented towards economic, environmental and social performance. The objective of the paper is to identify the main opportunities and challenges generated by the integration of ERP systems and artificial intelligence in the financial and accounting activities undertaken by organizations, as well as to highlight the impact on the accounting profession and the decision-making process. The research method used to quantify the key findings relevant to the topic of this article was qualitative, focusing on the responses received from various respondents during interviews conducted with them. The results indicated a high degree of satisfaction of users in the financial-accounting field regarding the generation and analysis of financial and non-financial information, as well as the automation of repetitive activities, the detection of various anomalies and risks, and the monitoring of ESG indicators. The results also highlighted the standardization of data collection processes, the integration of financial and non-financial information into a single platform, the development of digital skills of accounting professionals and auditors, and the promotion of an organizational culture favorable to innovation and change. Thus, the study proposed in this article focuses on providing relevant information for both academia and practitioners or specialists in the financial-accounting and auditing fields regarding the building of intelligent, resilient and sustainable development-oriented organizations.

title: Who Governs Carbon? Board Diversity and Incentive‐Linked Pay as Key Drivers of Disclosure in FTSE 100 Firms
summary: ABSTRACT Corporate boards are increasingly expected to drive climate accountability, yet evidence on which governance mechanisms shape carbon transparency remains contradictory. Using an unbalanced panel of 618 firm‐year observations from 62 FTSE 100 nonfinancial firms (2015–2025), this study examines how board structure, composition and incentive design shape both the decision to disclose carbon emissions via the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) and the depth of that disclosure (a 0–8 quality scale). Combining pooled OLS, fixed‐effects, random‐effects and logit regressions with structural equation modelling, we find that gender diversity and sustainability‐linked executive compensation are the only governance mechanisms consistently and robustly associated with both disclosure outcomes; board size is positively associated with disclosure depth but not with the disclosure decision itself. Board independence, meeting frequency, attendance and sustainability committees show no material effect once firm‐specific heterogeneity is controlled for. Structural equation modelling further reveals a negative covariance between governance and financial‐capacity constructs, suggesting a long‐term sustainability trade‐off. These findings extend recent cross‐country meta‐analytic evidence by showing that, once structural governance adoption is near‐universal, incremental gains in carbon transparency come from incentive alignment and compositional diversity rather than additional structural apparatus. For policymakers, investors and boards, the implication is that diversity targets and ESG‐linked pay are more reliable levers of carbon transparency than procedural governance metrics.

title: Does Financial Slack Matter? Corporate Governance, Corporate Activities, And Sustainability Reporting Quality in Indonesia
summary: This study examines the effects of corporate governance mechanisms and asset turnover on sustainability reporting quality, with particular emphasis on the moderating role of financial slack. Drawing on agency, legitimacy, and stakeholder theories, the study employs a quantitative approach using panel data from 33 companies consistently included in Indonesia's ESGQ-KEHATI Index between 2021 and 2024, yielding 132 firm-year observations. Sustainability reporting quality is assessed through content analysis of 33 environmental, social, and governance (ESG) indicators, while financial slack is measured as the ratio of free cash flow to total revenue. The data are analyzed using fixed-effects panel regression and moderated regression analysis. The findings reveal that the proportion of independent commissioners, audit committee, and total asset turnover positively and significantly influence sustainability reporting quality, whereas managerial ownership has no significant effect. Financial slack exhibits a positive direct association with reporting quality and strengthens the effects of independent commissioners and the audit committee, but does not significantly moderate the relationships involving managerial ownership or asset turnover. The adjusted R² increases from 0.514 to 0.533 following the inclusion of financial slack in the regression specification. Firm age is positively associated with reporting quality, while firm size has no significant effect. These findings suggest that financial flexibility complements formal corporate governance oversight in improving sustainability reporting quality. The study contributes to sustainability governance literature by demonstrating that the moderating role of financial slack differs across governance and operational mechanisms, highlighting the importance of resource availability in supporting effective sustainability oversight.

title: Heterogeneous effects of green finance, governance, and geopolitical risk on renewable energy consumption in G7 economies
summary: This study examines the effects of environmental policy stringency, green finance, geopolitical risk, governance, economic growth, and inequalities on renewable energy consumption across G7 economies (2003–2023). Employing Quantile Method of Moments Regression (QMMR) and Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality tests, the analysis captures heterogeneous dynamics across energy transition stages. Findings indicate that policy stringency, green finance, governance quality, and economic growth drive renewable energy consumption, with regulatory and financial mechanisms exerting the strongest impacts at lower-to-middle quantiles. Conversely, geopolitical risk dampens renewable consumption, particularly at higher quantiles due to heightened investment uncertainty and supply chain vulnerabilities. Income and gender inequalities exhibit marginal effects, confirming that institutional capacity and regulatory frameworks predominate in advanced economies. Ultimately, the results underscore the need for stage-differentiated policy mixes integrating green finance, robust governance, and risk mitigation to advance clean energy targets (SDGs 7, 10, and 13).

title: Islamic Ethics in the Digital Era: A Bibliometric Analysis
summary: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has introduced complex ethical challenges that require critical examination through religious and moral perspectives, including Islamic ethics. This study aims to systematically map the intellectual structure, research development, collaborative networks, and emerging thematic trends in scholarly literature concerning Islamic ethics in the digital era. Employing a bibliometric approach, the study utilizes VOSviewer to conduct citation analysis, co-authorship analysis, institutional and country collaboration mapping, keyword co-occurrence analysis, overlay visualization, and density visualization. The findings reveal that Islamic digital ethics constitutes an increasingly interdisciplinary research domain encompassing artificial intelligence, digital communication, Islamic finance, blockchain, and sustainable digital transformation. Citation analysis identifies blockchain, financial technology, and Islamic finance as influential areas of scholarly contribution. The collaboration analysis demonstrates the prominent roles of Indonesia and Malaysia in international research networks, although institutional collaboration remains relatively concentrated. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies artificial intelligence, Islamic ethics, digital ethics, social media, and ethical principles as dominant themes. Furthermore, overlay visualization indicates a thematic transition from digital financial applications and communication technologies toward machine learning, digital transformation, and sustainable development. Density visualization confirms the concentration of scholarly attention around artificial intelligence and ethical frameworks while revealing comparatively less developed thematic areas. The study highlights the importance of integrating Islamic ethical principles, particularly trustworthiness, justice, accountability, and public welfare, into contemporary technological governance. These findings contribute to the literature by providing a systematic understanding of the field's intellectual landscape and identifying potential directions for future interdisciplinary research on responsible artificial intelligence, data privacy, algorithmic accountability, and sustainable digital innovation.

title: Supply Chain Digitalization and Business Performance: The Role of Artificial Intelligence, IoT, and Data Analytics
summary: Supply chain digitalization has emerged as a major component of contemporary business transformation as organizations seek greater visibility, efficiency, resilience, responsiveness, and competitiveness across increasingly complex global supply networks. Artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and data analytics are among the principal technologies driving this transformation. This paper examines the relationship between supply chain digitalization and business performance, focusing specifically on how AI, IoT, and data analytics influence operational efficiency, forecasting accuracy, inventory management, logistics, supply chain visibility, risk management, customer service, resilience, and financial performance. The study adopts a systematic literature review and conceptual analytical approach to synthesize existing theoretical and empirical research. The analysis indicates that AI can strengthen forecasting, optimization, automation, predictive maintenance, supplier assessment, and decision-making; IoT technologies can improve real-time monitoring, traceability, asset utilization, and visibility; and data analytics can transform large volumes of operational information into predictive and prescriptive insights. Their combined use can create digitally integrated supply chains capable of responding more rapidly to market changes and disruptions. However, digital transformation also introduces challenges involving implementation costs, cybersecurity, data quality, legacy-system integration, interoperability, organizational resistance, skills shortages, privacy, and AI governance. The paper proposes an integrated conceptual framework in which AI capability, IoT connectivity, and dataanalytics capability strengthen supply chain visibility, agility, integration, and resilience, which subsequently influence operational and financial performance. The study concludes that technology alone does not guarantee superior business performance; value creation depends on strategic alignment, high-quality data, organizational capabilities, workforce skills, governance, cybersecurity, and effective integration across supply chain partners.

summary: La sostenibilidad corporativa bajo el enfoque Environmental, Social and Governance, ha puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de comprender el papel que desempeñan los sistemas internos de control en la generación de valor sostenible. title: ESG : Signal or Driver? Panel Evidence and Implications for Sustainable Business Strategy
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the ESG–firm performance relationship using panel analysis, a question with direct implications for sustainable investment strategy and corporate decision‐making. Using Refinitiv and S&P Global ESG scores matched to Compustat financials for approximately 1120 global firms over an 11‐year panel (2015–2025), we compare pooled OLS estimates with firm‐fixed‐effects specifications that control for time‐invariant unobserved heterogeneity. Results reveal that significant associations observed in the pooled OLS largely disappear with firm‐fixed effects across both ESG rating providers. Coefficients shrink by 65%–133% and lose statistical significance across the four performance outcome measures: gross profit margin, asset turnover, EV/Sales ratio, and Tobin's Q. The attenuation pattern holds under a series of robustness checks, including lagged ESG, difference GMM (Arellano‐Bond), and substituting Refinitiv with S&P Global ESG scores, which substantially reduces concern that the findings are provider‐specific. These findings do not provide evidence of a causal within‐firm relationship between ESG and firm performance when unobserved firm characteristics, such as management quality, organizational culture, and strategic positioning, are taken into consideration. Among many theoretical frameworks that could elucidate the relationship, our results align with signaling theory, that is, the evidence is more consistent with ESG functioning as a signal of underlying firm quality than a driver of financial outcomes. For sustainable finance practitioners, ESG scores may remain informative for quality screening, but our results provide little evidence that within‐firm improvements in ESG scores systematically generate corresponding improvements in the financial outcomes examined. For corporate strategy, capability‐building investments that authentically improve stakeholder relationships create more durable value than optimizing ESG metrics. For policymakers, our results caution against justifying ESG mandates solely on the assumption that improvements in ESG scores necessarily generate firm‐level financial gains; the case for such mandates rests more securely on societal benefits and externality correction.

title: Audit Committee Financial Expertise and Sustainability Reporting of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: Moderated by Women Chairperson
summary: Sustainability reporting has become an integral aspect of corporate governance as stakeholders increasingly demand transparency regarding environmental, social, and governance performance. In the Nigerian banking sector, Deposit Money Banks are strategically positioned to promote sustainable finance; however, sustainability disclosures remain uneven across institutions. This study examines the effect of audit committee financial expertise on sustainability reporting of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, while assessing the moderating role of audit committee women chairperson. The study adopted an ex‑post facto research design using secondary data extracted from the audited annual reports of all fourteen (14) listed DMBs in Nigeria for the period 2010–2024. Data were analysed using panel regression techniques with the aid of STATA. Findings revealed that audit committee financial expertise has a positive and statistically significant effect on sustainability reporting. The presence of a woman chairperson on the audit committee was also found to significantly enhance sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, the moderating effect of audit committee women chairperson on the relationship between audit committee financial expertise and sustainability reporting was statistically significant. The study concludes that audit committee financial expertise significantly enhances the quality of sustainability reporting among Nigerian deposit money banks. Similarly, audit committee women chairperson contributes positively and does significantly moderate the effect of audit committee financial expertise on sustainability reporting. The study recommends that Nigerian banks should strengthen audit committees by appointing members with strong financial and accounting expertise. Similarly, Regulators should promote gender diversity and encourage women leadership among the audit committee to improve inclusivity and ethical governance.

title: Governance moderators on the nexus between FinTech and ESG disclosure in Saudi banks
summary: This study examines the association between FinTech disclosure and environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure in Saudi banks and further unfolds the moderating role of board independence (IND) and sustainability committees (SUS_C). Using a balanced panel of 10 listed banks from 2015 to 2024, we measure FinTech disclosure from annual-report keyword frequencies and obtain ESG and pillar scores from Bloomberg. The primary bank fixed-effects estimates indicate positive associations between FinTech disclosure and overall ESG disclosure, particularly its social and governance pillars. Evidence concerning the environmental pillar emerges only after governance moderators are considered. In the combined model, the FinTech × IND × SUS_C coefficient is statistically insignificant for overall ESG, social and governance disclosure, while its positive association with environmental disclosure provides only initial evidence of joint moderation. Conditional marginal effects and supplementary two-way fixed-effects analyses using bank-clustered, Driscoll-Kraay and wild-cluster bootstrap inference do not consistently confirm the environmental result. The findings therefore provide suggestive and estimator-sensitive evidence that governance structure may condition the relationship between FinTech and ESG disclosure. The study contributes evidence from an emerging-market banking system to the literature on FinTech, ESG disclosure and corporate governance.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Corporate ESG Performance: Causal Evidence from Machine Learning Methods
summary: This study examines the effect of artificial intelligence (AI) innovation on corporate ESG performance in Chinese listed firms. Using 42,996 firm-year observations of 4792 A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we measure AI innovation by AI patent applications and ESG performance by Huazheng ESG ratings. Two-way fixed effects estimates indicate that a one-unit increase in ln(1 + AI patent applications) is associated with a 0.037-point increase in the ESG score, or about 5% of a standard deviation for a one-standard-deviation increase in AI. Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML) estimates with firm-level cross-fitting are similar (0.026–0.038). The relationship is robust to lagged AI, predetermined controls, ordinal and rank-based outcomes, and an event-study design that shows no differential ESG trends before firms’ first AI patent application; however, it is driven by the intensity of AI patenting rather than by the extensive margin and is imprecisely estimated within the pre- and post-2017 disclosure regimes. Mechanism tests suggest efficiency and internal-control channels, whereas the management expense ratio does not mediate the effect. The effect is stronger in larger firms and in firms with greater green innovation capability and tends to be larger in more market-oriented regions (significant at the 10% level), while the difference between heavily polluting and other firms is not statistically significant. Under a conditional exogeneity assumption, these results are consistent with a causal effect of AI innovation on ESG performance.
