title: ESG legitimacy games in retail management: balancing symbolic compliance and entrepreneurial legitimacy under policy and public pressure in China
summary: This study examines the structural misalignment of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) priorities among policy guidance, public attention, and corporate responses in China. Drawing on agenda-setting and legitimacy theory, it introduces a structural deviation index, a quantitative measure capturing the divergence among policy orientation, public concern, and firm-level ESG performance across E, S, and G dimensions. Using policy text analysis, Baidu Index data, and ESG ratings of 3,030 listed firms from 2019 to 2023, three pairwise distances – Policy–Corporate, Public–Corporate, and Policy–Public – are constructed. The results show that Policy–Corporate Distance is consistently the largest, indicating a significant gap between regulatory priorities and corporate behavior. The environmental dimension exhibits the greatest misalignment despite strong policy emphasis, while firms align more closely with public attention in social issues. Overall, firms tend to adopt symbolic compliance strategies, prioritizing low-cost governance and social initiatives over substantive environmental transformation. The findings also reflect emerging trends in social computing through digitally expressed public attention and their relevance to customer relationship management. For retail organizations, these findings offer strategic and operational applications for aligning ESG practices with consumer expectations, while providing managerial applications for strengthening market positioning, competitive differentiation, and customer relationships.

title: Does Going Green Change the Numbers? Carbon Footprint Certification, Corporate Governance, and Firm Outcomes in Thailand
summary: ABSTRACT Voluntary environmental certification is often assumed to signal broader improvements in corporate accountability, including financial reporting quality. This study tests that assumption using Thailand's Carbon Footprint for Organization (CFO) certification, a third‐party‐verified carbon‐accounting scheme administered by the country's Greenhouse Gas Management Organization. We ask whether certification is associated with earnings quality and financial performance among Stock Exchange of Thailand‐listed non‐financial firms, and whether firm‐level corporate governance moderates this relationship. Using a staggered difference‐in‐differences design on a propensity‐score‐matched panel of 409 firms over fiscal years 2013–2024, we triangulate four estimators of increasing robustness to bias—a naive baseline, stacked two‐way fixed effects with contaminated comparisons removed, and two heterogeneity‐robust staggered‐adoption estimators—so that our conclusions do not rest on any single method's assumptions; governance moderation is tested using a hand‐collected, seven‐component governance index measured before certification. Certification shows no detectable effect on earnings management, accrual quality, or accounting profitability, and interval and equivalence tests rule out effects larger than roughly 0.3 standard deviations for each outcome. Market valuation is the one exception: certified firms show a positive association with Tobin's Q , but this result is weak and specification‐dependent, and does not survive alternative comparison groups or multiple‐testing adjustment. Governance moderation is likewise exploratory: a few raw signals emerge when governance is measured before certification, but none survives correction for multiple testing. These patterns are consistent with certification that is genuinely implemented yet decoupled from internal financial‐reporting behavior, extending institutional accounts of voluntary certification and signaling theory. Because our outcomes capture financial‐reporting spillovers rather than the scheme's environmental ends, we cannot speak to whether certification changes environmental practice itself. For policymakers and investors, the findings caution against inferring improved financial‐reporting quality, or genuine environmental commitment, from certification status alone.

title: A SHAP-Based Nonlinear Analysis Approach to Audit Identification of Patient Capital
summary: Patient capital, with its strong financial capacity and risk prevention advantages, safeguards high-risk innovative enterprises and also influences auditors’ professional judgment. Using a sample of Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed companies from 2011 to 2024, this paper investigates whether auditors can recognize the risk prevention effects of patient capital and thereby reduce audit pricing. The findings reveal that patient capital significantly reduces audit fees. Mechanism tests show that patient capital lowers audit pricing by reducing auditors’ business risk and audit risk. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the inhibitory effect of patient capital on audit pricing is more pronounced in firms with low ownership concentration, high market competition, and those undergoing digital transformation. Further SHAP-based nonlinear analysis demonstrates that auditors’ risk perceptions of the two types of patient capital differ fundamentally: debt capital exerts governance effects only within a certain leverage range, and pushes pricing upward beyond the threshold, exhibiting a “threshold response” pattern; equity capital exhibits diminishing marginal effects as scale expands, displaying a “safety cushion” pattern. This study enriches the research on the economic consequences of patient capital investment and the determinants of audit pricing, providing a reference for auditors to identify the advantages of patient capital.

title: Behavioral Choice Architecture in Digital Finance: A Comparative Bibliometric Review of Nudges, Sludges, and Responsible FinTech Across Emerging and Developed Economies
summary: Digital financial platforms increasingly embed behavioral choice architecture—nudges, gamification, and occasionally sludges—whose welfare consequences vary with institutional context. This study reports a comparative bibliometric and structured content-analysis review of 97 peer-reviewed articles (2016–2026) retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus following PRISMA 2020, integrating performance analysis, science mapping, and welfare-oriented coding of 90 full-text records across emerging (EM) and developed (DM) markets. Production grew sharply after 2024, accounting for 69.1% of output, with EM settings representing 56.7% of the corpus. Gamification dominated the field (57.7% of records at screening; 54.4% of primary interventions after full-text coding), substantially outpacing conventional nudges (17.5–21.1%) and explicit sludge or dark-pattern research (3.1–3.3%), and was 2.67 times more prevalent in EM than DM studies (64.0% versus 24.0%), the only EM–DM difference that remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Co-citation analysis identified two intellectual communities—gamified digital-banking adoption and gamification motivation and continuance—both anchored in information-systems and service-marketing adoption research, while foundational behavioral-economics works remained outside the citation core. Behavioral effectiveness was documented far more often than welfare outcomes, and no retrieved study focused primarily on the exit stage of the digital consumer journey, a gap that persisted in a complementary search targeting sludge and exit terminology. These findings indicate that digital-finance nudging has developed primarily as an engagement-design phenomenon rather than a welfare-economics one, calling for differentiated EM/DM safeguards and urgent research on exit architecture and dark patterns as financial-services regulation begins to outpace the evidence base.

title: Digital transformation and customer loyalty: The mediating role of co-created service experience in Indonesian banking
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractBanks invest in digital platforms expecting stronger loyalty. Yet, it remains unclear why some investments build durable relationships while others do not, because prior research conflates what customers do with how they experience it. This study tests whether co-created service experience mediates the relationship between customer-perceived digital transformation and customer loyalty among digital banking customers in Indonesia. Survey data were collected in 2025 from 360 customers of five banks in Medan, Indonesia, who had used mobile or internet banking for at least six months, ensuring direct experience with digital banking, and were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping. All four hypotheses were supported: digital transformation was strongly associated with co-created service experience (β = 0.659, p < 0.001) and significantly associated with loyalty directly (β = 0.425, p < 0.001); co-created service experience was significantly associated with loyalty (β = 0.478, p < 0.001) and partially mediated the digital transformation–loyalty relationship (indirect effect β = 0.315, p < 0.001; VAF = 42.6%), with the model explaining 67.8% of the variance in loyalty. Digital transformation is thus associated with loyalty through two distinct routes, only one of which depends on customers feeling like genuine participants. Institutional trust was not measured directly in this study, so the link between this pattern and Indonesia's institutional trust conditions is interpretive and requires further testing. Because the sample is limited to a single city, findings apply to this market and should not be generalized to Indonesian banking as a whole.

title: Digital economy and synergy effect of pollution reduction and carbon emission reduction: Based on the threshold effect analysis of environmental penalty and pollution intensity
summary: Abstract Under the dual circumstances of the “dual carbon” goal promotion and the deep development of the digital economy (DE), clarifying the influence mechanism of the DE on the synergy effect of pollution reduction and carbon emission reduction (SEPRCER) is of great practical significance for promoting the green and high-quality development of the region. This paper is based on the panel data of 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB) from 2011 to 2023. It systematically analyzes the evolution characteristics of the DE and the SEPRCER, and empirically examines the influencing mechanism between the two. The results show: (1) The level of the DE in the YREB shows an overall upward trend, while the level of the SEPRCER shows a slight downward trend. Both form a distribution pattern with the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) as the core and multiple growth poles coexisting in space; (2) The influence of the DE on the SEPRCER presents a significant "U" shape relationship, and this conclusion still holds after robustness and endogeneity tests; (3) The relationship between the two shows heterogeneity characteristics. The “U” shape feature is more prominent in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River (LRYR), urban agglomerations, non-resource-based cities, and regions with high economic levels; (4) Both the environmental protection penalty intensity (EPPI) and the pollution intensity (PI) exhibit a significant single-threshold. As the EPPI crosses the threshold value, the turning point of the “U” shape curve for the DE and the SEPRCER will be reached earlier, while the opposite is true for the PI; (5) From the two threshold variables interaction grouping perspective, in the combination of high EPPI and low PI, the “U” shaped inflection points for the DE and the SEPRCER is the earliest. The research conclusions provide theoretical basis for improving the SEPRCER in the YREB.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF MSMEs THROUGH SOCIAL COMMERCE TRAINING AND MENTORING TO INCREASE BUSINESS REVENUE
summary: Digital transformation is an important strategy for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their competitiveness and expand their marketing reach, including those providing barbershop services. The partner enterprise had not fully utilized social media for marketing and social commerce to increase customer numbers and business revenue. This community service program aimed to improve barbershop operators’ knowledge and skills in using social commerce through participatory training and mentoring. The program employed a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach comprising four stages: planning, action, observation, and reflection. Activities included problem identification, digital strategy planning, content creation training, hands-on social media management, mentoring in marketing strategy implementation, and monitoring and evaluation. The results indicated improvements in the partner’s understanding and skills in managing social media, creating promotional content, building customer interactions, and utilizing digital media to support the marketing of barbershop services. The implementation of social commerce also offered opportunities to expand market reach, increase consumer engagement, attract new customers, and support revenue growth. Sustained implementation of digital strategies is needed to maximize the program’s long-term benefits.

title: Digital Transformation of MSMEs: The Relationship Between Digital Literacy, AI Adoption, And Business Growth
summary: Background: MSMEs are central to Indonesia’s economy but face uneven digital capabilities, limited AI adoption, and persistent digital skills constraints. Despite their economic importance, many MSMEs continue to face limited digital capabilities, insufficient technology-oriented training, and uneven access to digital infrastructure, which can constrain the effective use of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI). Objective: This study examines the relationships among digital literacy, AI adoption, digital transformation, and MSME business performance in Bogor Regency. Methods: A mixed-methods sequential exploratory design was used, beginning with qualitative exploration and followed by a quantitative survey of 384 MSME respondents analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: Descriptive scores indicate relatively stronger digital transformation than AI adoption; however, the reported hypothesis-testing p-values for H1–H5 (0.313, 0.238, 0.138, 0.124, and 0.194) are all above 0.05 and therefore do not support claims of statistically significant direct effects at the conventional significance level. Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to distinguish descriptive digital readiness from statistically supported structural relationships and provide a basis for more rigorous model testing in MSME digitalization research.

title: Exploring the nexus between employee agility and digital transformation: a systematic literature review of recent trends in digital HRM
summary: The rapid advancement of Industry 4.0 technologies has revolutionized human resource management (HRM), accelerating its evolution from conventional digital HRM toward intelligent, data-driven smart practices. The transition to Smart HRM 4.0 signifies the relevant of employee agility when implementing strategies of digital HRM. To establish the link between employee agility and digital transformation, two research questions were formulated: (1) what new trends are emerging in the field of digital transformation through the prism of Smart HRM 4.0, and (2) what effect does employee agility have on the adoption of Smart HRM 4.0? Through PRISMA guidelines, this paper provides a systematic review of studies published between 2015 and 2025 in the Scopus journal database. According to the keywords search, 835 selected papers were screened for their relevance to the formulated research questions. Based on the screening process and inclusion and exclusion criteria, 11 papers have been found relevant for the review. Along with the established agility-adoption link, the analysis reveals that digital leadership, organisational culture, and digital literacy influence employee agility towards HR technology. Overall, this research underscores the significance of employee agility in adopting digital HRM and suggests further research on human-technology interaction in digital settings.

title: Legal and Organizational Aspects of the Transition to Mandatory Electronic Document Management in Accounting
summary: The relevance of this topic is determined by the fact that the mandatory use of the universal transfer document format 5.03 is planned to be regulated from 2026, while the legal regulation of the transition period contains certain gaps, and the organizational and technical readiness of market participants remains heterogeneous. The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive analysis of the legal and organizational conditions of the upcoming transition, systematize the implementation issues, and develop practical recommendations for economic entities. The scientific significance of the work is determined by the identification of contradictions between the norms of the basic law on accounting and departmental acts; the practical significance is determined by the development of an algorithm for preparing for the transition, which can be applied by organizations of various forms of ownership. The results of the study have shown that the digitalization of document management is a gradual process, and the economic effect is primarily achieved through the release of staff time. The identified legal gaps necessitate the adoption of a specialized federal accounting standard.

title: From Vulnerability to Resilience: Assessing Africa’s Climate Adaptation Strategies Under the Paris Agreement
summary: Africa remains one of the regions most vulnerable to climate change despite contributing a relatively small share of global greenhouse gas emissions. The Paris Agreement has elevated adaptation as a central component of international climate governance, particularly through its Global Goal on Adaptation and provisions relating to climate finance, technology transfer, and capacity building. This article assesses the effectiveness of Africa’s climate adaptation strategies under the Paris Agreement and examines the extent to which existing legal, policy, and institutional frameworks are translating international adaptation commitments into practical resilience outcomes. The study adopts a qualitative doctrinal methodology, complemented by a thematic review of selected adaptation practices and country experiences across Africa. The analysis finds significant progress in integrating adaptation into national and regional policy frameworks through climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem-based adaptation, water resource management, disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, and regional cooperation. However, effectiveness remains constrained by inadequate and unpredictable climate finance, institutional fragmentation, technological and capacity limitations, socioeconomic vulnerability, weak monitoring and accountability mechanisms, and insufficient community participation. The article concludes that formal policy commitments alone are insufficient to produce measurable resilience; effective implementation requires predictable adaptation finance, stronger domestic institutions, improved technology access, robust monitoring and evaluation, enhanced regional cooperation, and meaningful participation of local communities and indigenous knowledge holders.

title: The External Reach of EU Labour Law: Channels of Influence and the Case of Vietnam
summary: This article examines how EU labour-law standards influence labour-related compliance beyond EU territory, despite the predominantly territorial character of public enforcement. It addresses the mismatch between the EU's state-centred enforcement framework and the transnational organisation of production, in which labour risks frequently arise in third-country supply chains. The aim of the article is to conceptualise ``external reach'' and to assess the main channels through which EU labour-related expectations operate outside the Union. Methodologically, the article combines doctrinal analysis with conceptual clarification and applies this framework to the case of Vietnam. It identifies three principal channels of external reach: labour provisions in EU trade agreements, outward-facing EU secondary legislation, and non-state or hybrid governance mechanisms, including contractual clauses, audits, and soft-law standards. The findings show that trade-related mechanisms are relatively effective in encouraging formal legal reform and regulatory dialogue, but have limited direct impact at workplace level. By contrast, market-facing mechanisms, especially due diligence obligations and private governance tools, more directly affect supplier behaviour, although they also risk procedural compliance, cost shifting, and weak accountability.

title: Impact of the Digital Economy on Women's Economic Empowerment in Flexible Employment: Evidence From the Chinese General Social Survey (2012–2021)
summary: ABSTRACT The digital economy stimulates economic growth and offers new opportunities for women's flexible employment. Utilizing the “Resources‐Agency‐Achievements” economic empowerment theory and data from the Chinese General Social Survey (2012–2021), alongside provincial digital economy development data, this study estimates a fixed‐effects instrumental‐variable (FE‐IV) model to analyze the digital economy's impact on women's economic empowerment in flexible employment. Digital economic development significantly boosts this empowerment, and the KHB results are consistent with a mediating role for gender role attitudes. Post‐2015, following the “Internet Plus” initiative, the empowerment effect intensified, especially benefiting women with urban registration, higher education, and higher incomes. However, women aged 40 and older experience fewer benefits, and entrepreneurial activity is negatively associated with digital economy development. The study constructs a composite empowerment index and examines gender role attitudes as a mediator, thus expanding the theoretical framework. Policy recommendations include enhancing digital skills training, improving social security for flexible employment, developing women‐friendly digital tools, and promoting female success stories.

title: Effects of HRM Gaps on Exploratory Innovation in the Context of Digital Transformation: Based on Institutional Logic Theory
summary: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, emerging market firms are undergoing profound structural adjustments. However, existing studies paid insufficient attention to how the gaps between human resource management implementation and employee perceptions affect exploratory innovation within the context of digital transformation. Drawing on institutional logic theory, we employ the multilevel polynomial regression and response surface analysis to examine the effect and mechanism of the human resource management gaps on employees’ exploratory innovation, with dataset collected from 83 companies in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region of China. We show that: (a) the significant human resource management gaps directly influence employees’ exploratory innovation; (b) the “high implementation-high perception” scenario yields the strongest employees’ exploratory innovation; (c) when the gaps are significant, its relationship with employees’ exploratory innovation follows an inverted U-shape; (d) uniqueness of human capital mediates the relationship between the human resource management gaps and employees’ exploratory innovation; (e) corporate digital maturity negatively moderates the relationship between the human resource management gaps and employees’ exploratory innovation. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for designing management policies that encourage exploratory innovation in the context of digital transformation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Higher Education: A Systematic Review of Opportunities, Challenges and Emerging Trends
summary: Artificial Intelligence AI is getting more and more involved in higher education, it is reshaping teaching, learning , assessment, academic administration, research, and even how institutions decide things. In the last few years the fast rise of generative artificial intelligence GenAI, plus intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, automated assessment, recommendation systems, and AI assisted administrative tools has opened up new possibilities for universities, yet it also brings worries like academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, digital inequality, transparency, and changing professional roles. This paper actually uses a secondary-data based systematic review, looking at research and policy sources about AI and digital transformation in higher education. The review brings together outcomes from academic studies, other systematic reviews, and international policy frameworks, sort of to map out the main uses, opportunities, obstacles, and the kind of emerging trends that are starting to show up. What the literature suggests is that AI in education is not only about making content. It also includes adaptive learning, personalized tutoring, intelligent assessment, profiling and prediction, and support for institutional management. At the same time, good adoption does not just happen, it needs institutional policies, AI literacy, ethical safety nets, teacher professional development, careful responsible assessment approaches, and a human centered way of putting things into practice. A number of recent international frameworks stress human agency, ethics, AI competencies, and responsible usage, so there is a clear direction there. Overall the review shows that AI is best understood as augmentation tech with AI to help educators and learners not to flip a switch and replace the educational roles that already exist. For digital transformation a balance must exist, with technical novelty on one side and pedagogical sense together with ethical norms institutional realities and human factors, on the other. None of those should be treated as optional because leaving one out tends to break the system quickly.

title: Digital Transformation and Management Capability in National Defense Posture: The Moderating Role of Defense Industry Self-Reliance
summary: Digital transformation has become central to defense modernization, yet evidence remains limited on how digital capabilities and management capacity interact with national defense-industry self-reliance to shape national defense posture. This study examines the direct effects of digital transformation, management capability, and defense-industry self-reliance, and tests whether self-reliance changes the effects of digital transformation and management capability on defense posture. The conceptual model integrates Dynamic Capability Theory, which explains organizational sensing, seizing, and transformation processes, with the Resource-Based View, which emphasizes strategic resource endowments. A cross-sectional survey produced 225 usable responses from personnel and officials associated with Indonesian defense institutions. The constructs were measured with 90 perception-based items and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with bootstrapping and predictive assessment. Digital transformation had the strongest positive direct effect on national defense posture, followed by management capability and defense-industry self-reliance. Defense-industry self-reliance significantly weakened the positive relationship between digital transformation and defense posture, contrary to the predicted direction, while it strengthened the relationship between management capability and defense posture. The model explained 75.4 percent of the variance in national defense posture and showed substantial out-of-sample predictive relevance. The negative moderation indicates that industrial localization can create short-term compatibility, resource-allocation, certification, and implementation frictions when domestic capabilities are not synchronized with digital modernization. The study contributes by showing that strategic resources do not automatically amplify dynamic capabilities; their value depends on alignment and implementation timing. Policy should therefore prioritize interoperable digital architectures, phased localization, technology-transfer milestones, and managerial capability development so that industrial self-reliance complements rather than constrains digital defense transformation.

title: The Influence of Corporate Governance on Financial Statements of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: The study sought to explore the impact of corporate governance on financial statement quality among listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. In particular, the impact of audit committee effectiveness, CEO duality, and ownership structure on financial statement quality was explored in the study. The study was based on the Stakeholder Theory, which suggests that organizations have an obligation to disclose accurate and reliable information to all stakeholders. The study applied the ex-post facto design and used secondary data collected from annual reports of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria from the year 2015 to 2025. Multiple regression analysis was conducted to determine the relationship between corporate governance variables and financial statement quality. The results indicated that audit committee effectiveness positively and significantly influences financial statement quality due to the fact that audit committees comprising of financially literate and independent members increase financial transparency and reporting accuracy. CEO duality, on the other hand, was found to negatively influence financial statement quality significantly.Moreover, there is evidence that ownership structure significantly and positively affects financial statement quality, hence implying that good monitoring of the ownership structure, especially from institutional investors, leads to higher quality disclosure and lower manager’s opportunistic behavior. According to the regression analysis, corporate governance had a strong combined explanatory power, explaining 61.0% of the variations in financial statement quality. This study thus finds that corporate governance is an essential element in improving financial statement quality, transparency, and reliability among listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. Corporate governance codes should be more strictly adhered to, audit committees need to be more efficient, the roles of board chairmen and CEOs should be separated, and more institutional ownership participation should be encouraged

title: Effect of Corporate Environmental Disclosure on Investor Decisions in the Oil and Gas Sector in Nigeria
summary: Backgrounds: Corporate environmental disclosure is increasingly important to investors, yet Nigerian studies examine it only in aggregate, obscuring which specific dimensions drive investor response. Objectives: This study specifically assesses the effects of environmental policies and practices disclosure, environmental expenditures and investments disclosure, GHG emissions disclosure, compliance with environmental regulations disclosure, and environmental audits and certifications disclosure on market capitalization. Methodology: The study adopted a quantitative correlational research design using secondary panel data drawn from the annual reports, sustainability reports, and financial statements of all 13 oil and gas companies, covering the five-year period 2019 to 2023 (65 firm-year observations). A binary content-analysis disclosure checklist was used to construct an index score for each disclosure dimension, and data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and panel regression. Findings: Environmental policies and practices disclosure (β = .34, p < .001), GHG emissions disclosure (β = .29, p < .01), and environmental audits and certifications disclosure (β = .31, p < .001) each had significant positive effects on market capitalization, while environmental expenditures and investments disclosure (β = .18, p < .05) and compliance with environmental regulations disclosure (β = .21, p < .01) also showed significant, comparatively smaller positive effects. Conclusions: Corporate environmental disclosure across all five dimensions is significantly and positively associated with market capitalization, with policy disclosure and third-party audit certification exerting the strongest effects. Firms should strengthen policy communication and pursue independent audits and certifications, while regulators should standardize disclosure requirements.

title: Digital Transformation for Sustainable Tourism: Evaluating the Role of Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, and Smart Technologies in Destination Management
summary: Tourism growth has intensified pressure on destinations through congestion, resource demand and greenhouse gas emissions, while digital technologies are rapidly changing how destinations are managed. This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI), big data and smart technologies can support sustainable destination management, focusing on four functions: visitor management, reduction of resource consumption, monitoring of environmental impacts, and sustainable tourism planning. Using an integrative narrative review of a purposive corpus of 25 peer-reviewed studies and institutional reports, the article (i) maps digital technologies to destination-management functions (Table 1), (ii) proposes a conceptual framework linking data sources, analytics, management functions and sustainability outcomes (Figure 1), and (iii) derives indicators for evaluating digital interventions (Table 2). The synthesis suggests that the evidence is strongest for visitor-behaviour sensing and demand forecasting, and more conceptual and fragmented for resource and environmental benefits. Digital tools can improve the timeliness and spatial precision of decisions, but they do not by themselves address structural drivers such as growth in tourism consumption, and they introduce risks of data bias, privacy loss, and the energy footprint of AI. The article argues that digital transformation contributes to sustainability when it is embedded in governance, combined with demand-management and decarbonization policy, and evaluated against outcome indicators rather than technology adoption.

title: Comparison of the Role of Financial Inclusion, Financial Technology, and Institutional Quality on the Growth of MSMEs in Indonesia and Malaysia
summary: The growth of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) is influenced by various factors, including financial inclusion, financial technology (fintech), and institutional quality. Although these three factors have been widely studied, comparative research comparing their roles in Indonesia and Malaysia is still limited. This study aims to analyze and compare the role of financial inclusion, financial technology, and institutional quality on the growth of MSMEs in both countries. The research uses a qualitative approach with a comparative design. Data is obtained through documentation techniques sourced from scientific articles, government reports, international organization publications, and relevant policy documents. Data analysis is carried out qualitatively through data reduction, data presentation, conclusion drawn, and strengthened by source triangulation to increase the credibility of findings. The results of the study show that financial inclusion, financial technology, and institutional quality have an important role in encouraging the growth of MSMEs in Indonesia and Malaysia. Malaysia has shown excellence in institutional quality, financial inclusion levels, and maturity of the fintech ecosystem, while Indonesia is experiencing rapid development but still faces challenges in equitable access to financing, financial literacy, and institutional effectiveness. These findings show that the growth of MSMEs requires synergy between expanding access to finance, strengthening digital innovation, and improving institutional quality. This research contributes through a cross-border comparative perspective that can be the basis for policy formulation in strengthening a sustainable MSME ecosystem.

title: Beyond Digital Adoption: How Digital Transformation Drives SME Growth, Productivity, and Market Expansion in Emerging Economies — A Systematic Literature Review and Empirical Synthesis
summary: Small and Medium Enterprises(SMEs) are the backbone of developing countries, generating significant employment, innovation, and Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Despite their potential to grow, they are resource-scarce, locked-out-of the market, and demonstrate low efficiency. Digital transformation (DT) is the focal point during a phase when the remedies are implemented, through which creating good oil for competitiveness and stimulate sustainable development. This research summarized empirical evidence and established the impacts of DT on SME economic performance in emerging countries. Based on a thorough synthesis of recent research papers from institutions and universities, empirical critical contribution of this research is the strong positive relationships between DT and economic indicators like sales increase, business process efficiency, and new markets development. In very broad terms, a 10% enhancement of digitization will generate a 1.35% general increase in GDP per capita for developing countries. Dynamic capability theory has been adopted to demonstrate that implementation of digitization enables firms to sound off their sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring capability to adapt to a turbulent environment. Among the major figures, the effects of fully fitted firmware for reporting revenue increase are 10%. The paper points out the major barriers to implementation, which could include lack of digital skills and high investments needed during the founding phase. In summary, the paper concludes with recommendations for policy actions for stimulating an inclusive digital framework to guarantee the maximum economic returns of DT for SMEs in emerging countries.

title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Economic Growth in India
summary: Abstract: The country is witnessing an unprecedented change in how economic activities are conceived, produced and used, mostly as a result of the increasing adoption of digital technologies. Digital platforms, financial transactions over the internet, technology companies, digital markets and non-financial services enabled by technology are rapidly becoming part of the Indian economy. Keeping these factors in mind, the present study aims to analyze the impact of digital economy growth on sustainable economic growth in India. The study takes into account the potential effects of digitalisation on the economic productivity, business efficiency, entrepreneurship, employment creation, financial engagement and access to economic opportunities. It also acknowledges that the advantages of digital development are not evenly distributed, as disparities in internet access, digital skills, technological infrastructure, affordability and cyber security remain to be a challenge for some parts of society. The paper reviews the opportunities and constraints of digital transformation of the Indian Economy with the help of the secondary data available from relevant government publications, institutional reports and published studies. The study contends that a pro-poor approach to infrastructure, human-capital building, and data stewardship, along with equal access to digital services, can help to drive continued economic growth with the help of digitalisation. India's digital transformation therefore is not just a technological shift but an integral part of India's journey towards inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
summary: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience, and customer emotional intelligence) lead to strengthening the fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities. Also, the pivotal phenomenon (fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities), individual-marketing factors, and technological factors lead to strengthening customer acumen (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors). Finally, it was determined that customer intelligence (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors) leads to a reduction in undesirable behavioral-reactive outcomes and a strengthening of desirable behavioral-reactive outcomes.Originality/Value: According to the results obtained from the implementation of the qualitative and quantitative parts of the research, the variables 1) deceptive advertising, 2) customer emotional intelligence, 3) customer respect for the brand, 4) buyer confusion, 5) brand uniqueness, 6) brand community, 7) brand love, 8) brand attachment, 9) customer thirst for shopping, 10) market rumor management, 11) digital age, 12) negative internal emotions, 13) customer mental anxiety, 14) interaction-communication problems, and 15) customer resentment, 16) brand responsibility are considered new research findings.

title: Digital Transformation as a Driver for Adapting Russian State Institutions to Support Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises: the Concept of “Digital Partner State”
summary: The article is devoted to the concept of a “digital partner state”, in which Russian public institutions supporting small and medium-size enterprises (SMEs) are not just an operational efficiency instrument but an institutional adaptation fundamental driver. The study scientific hypothesis is digital transformation is not limited to automation of Russian SME support institutions functions, but is seen as an active transformation key factor, ensuring the transition to the concept “digital partner state”. On the basis of a theoretical approaches comprehensive analysis and Russian practice, the main stages and results of Russian SME support institutions digital transformation has been systemized, including the Digital Platform SME. RF creation, the development of “My Business” centers and the implementation of a Common Register of Control Activities. The research scientific novelty lies in: developing the “digital partner state” concept in relation to the Russian field of SME support; developing an authorial typology of interaction models between the state and business in a digital environment; identifying and systematizing the institutional effects of digital transformation (in particular, the transition to a “digital partner state” model helps bridge communication gaps, reduce transaction costs, and ensure synergies between support measures); and in the systemic analysis of the whole set of digital institutions and key normative acts (Government Commission on Digital Development, Ministry of Economic Development of Russia, Ministry of Civil Affairs of Russia, RFRIT, Fund for Innovation Promotion, "Skolkovo" Foundation, FRI, SME Corporation, "My Business" centers, SME platforms, "Public Services", supplier portal, "SME Business Navigator", as well as laws 478 FZ, 248 FZ, 258 FS) as a single institutional environment.

title: DETERMINAN PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN GENERASI Z DI DESA TUNGGARA, BANJARNEGARA
summary: Sound financial management is an essential competence for Generation Z, who grow up in a digital environment with heavy exposure to consumption trends. This study examines the effects of financial literacy, hedonistic lifestyle, self-control, Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), and financial technology (fintech) on the financial management of Generation Z in Tunggara Village, Banjarnegara Regency. A quantitative survey design was used. Primary data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire distributed via Google Forms to 100 respondents aged 16–29 years, selected by purposive sampling from a population of 479, and analyzed with multiple linear regression. Financial literacy (B = 0.591; p < 0.001), self-control (B = 0.165; p < 0.001), and fintech (B = 0.142; p = 0.010) have positive and significant effects on financial management, whereas hedonistic lifestyle (p = 0.614) and FoMO (p = 0.675) have no significant effect. The model is feasible (F = 57.954; p < 0.001) and explains 75.5% of the variance in financial management. Financial literacy is the most dominant determinant (standardized beta = 0.561). The findings highlight the need for applied financial education, stronger self-control, and prudent fintech use among rural Generation Z.

title: When Financial Reporting Readability Matters for Audit Effort: The Role of Conditional Conservatism
summary: This study examines whether conditional conservatism attenuates the additional audit effort associated with low financial reporting readability. Using 11,167 firm-year observations for 859 US non-financial firms listed on the New York Stock Exchange from 2010 to 2022, we estimate panel regressions with year and industry fixed effects. Readability is measured with five linguistic indices, audit effort is proxied by audit fees and audit delay, and conditional conservatism is captured through a firm-year asymmetric timeliness measure. Higher readability is associated with lower audit fees and shorter audit delays. More importantly, the positive interaction between readability and conditional conservatism indicates that these negative associations weaken as conditional conservatism increases. Drawing on agency and signalling theories, we interpret conservatism as an accounting-based mechanism that constrains optimistic reporting and enhances perceived reporting credibility. The study connects textual disclosure quality with accounting recognition practices and shows that auditors’ responses to narrative complexity depend partly on the properties of the underlying accounting numbers.

title: Top management attributes and market valuation across economic regimes: an ESG accountability signalling perspective from an emerging EU capital market
summary: Purpose This study examines whether the market-valuation associations attached to female and foreign executive representation, managerial interlocks and managerial ownership differ between stable and crisis periods, and whether the observed patterns are compatible with an Environmental, Social, and Corporate Governance (ESG) accountability-signalling perspective alongside competing governance interpretations. Design/methodology/approach The study uses Orbis data for non-financial Warsaw Stock Exchange firms over 2017–2023. Baseline difference and system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimates are supplemented by CRE/Mundlak and firm fixed-effects specifications. The governance variables are based on the available 2023 records, and treated as structurally persistent; main coefficients therefore rely primarily on cross-sectional differences between firms, while COVID interactions capture regime-contingent valuation differences. Findings In the baseline system GMM, female and foreign executive representation and managerial interlocks are positively associated with firm valuation during stable periods. Their COVID-period interactions are negative; combined COVID-period associations remain positive. The negative interactions for foreign executive representation and managerial interlocks remain statistically significant across alternative estimators, whereas the female-representation interaction is less robust. While the stable-period managerial–ownership polynomial is not jointly significant, its COVID interactions are so, indicating a regime difference in the polynomial association. Results are insensitive to governance-variable winsorisation but sensitive to the treatment of extreme Tobin’s Q values. Practical implications Observable governance profiles may carry valuation-relevant information, whose relevance varies across economic conditions. Our findings may inform how firms communicate governance arrangements but do not identify the investor mechanisms driving the observed regime differences. Originality/value The study documents regime-contingent valuation associations attached to structurally persistent governance profiles in an emerging EU capital market and evaluates them through an ESG accountability-signalling lens without excluding competing governance explanations.

title: Digital Cash-to-Cash Transformation and Organizational Resilience: Evidence from Working-Capital Buffer Configuration
summary: Abstract Digital transformation is increasingly important for firms seeking to remain resilient under conditions of uncertainty, yet less is known about how digital technologies strengthen resilience when they are embedded in specific operating routines. This study examines whether digital cash-to-cash transformation, the digital redesign and operational integration of inventory, receivables, and payables routines, enhances organisational resilience. Using Chinese listed firms from 2012 to 2024, we construct a large-language-model-based textual measure from annual reports that distinguishes substantive digital transformation in working-capital processes from generic digital disclosure. The results show that digital cash-to-cash transformation is positively associated with a multidimensional measure of organisational resilience. This finding remains robust to alternative measures, instrumental-variable estimation, propensity score matching, double machine learning, and shock-based tests. Mechanism analyses indicate that the resilience benefits of digital transformation arise primarily through working-capital buffer configuration rather than simple cash-cycle compression. Specifically, digital transformation is associated with higher inventory, receivables, and payables postures, each of which is positively related to resilience. The effects are stronger among more focused firms and firms pursuing differentiation strategies. These findings suggest that the resilience value of digital transformation lies not merely in adopting digital technologies, but in embedding them in cash-to-cash routines that improve information visibility, coordination, and the flexible deployment of working-capital resources.

title: Reconfiguring external and internal networks for resilience, agility and ambidexterity under geopolitical volatility
summary: Purpose Geopolitical tensions and economic policy volatility are compelling multinational firms to redesign both external supply chain networks and their intra-organisational networks of plants, subsidiaries and governance. This study examines how intra-organisational networks are redesigned in response to geopolitically induced reshaping of external supply chain networks and how this redesign enables resilience, agility and ambidexterity. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative multiple-case design with three longitudinal focal cases and five supporting cases. The data comprise 58 semi-structured interviews, supplemented by secondary documents to reconstruct case trajectories over time. Findings Geopolitically driven external network reshaping heightens dependence and power asymmetry through concentrated bottlenecks, low substitutability, and compliance-gated access. Firms respond through buffering, bridging, and selective internalisation, but these moves become effective only when internal decision rights, subsidiary mandates, and integration capacity are redesigned. Originality/value The study conceptualises external and intra-organisational network restructuring as a coupled, dependence-driven process under geopolitical volatility. It extends Resource Dependence Theory by showing that dependence-management strategies require internal re-architecture to become executable, thereby reframing resilience, agility, and ambidexterity as outcomes of organisational redesign rather than static capabilities.

title: Circular Economy and Competition: Merger Control and the Role of the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) in Integrating Sustainability into Brazil’s Competition Policy
summary: Abstract This article examines how the circular economy, as a sustainable economic model, can be integrated into Brazil’s free competition regime, focusing on the extent to which efficiencies linked to circular practices may be recognized under Brazilian merger control by the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE). The central research question is whether, and under what conditions, environmental and resource-efficiency benefits can be reconciled with the consumer welfare standard without undermining competitive dynamics. Initially, it contextualizes the relationship between competition and environmental protection according to the Federal Constitution, highlighting the principles of the economic order. It then explores the concept of the circular economy and its status in Brazil, analyzing public and private initiatives and correlating these practices with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies, demonstrating their competitive benefits. Based on an analysis of CADE’s decisions related to sustainability, the article proposes a reflection on how circular economy elements can be considered as efficiency factors in merger reviews. The central hypothesis is that incorporating circular economy criteria into CADE competition assessments can foster sustainable practices, generate economic and environmental efficiency gains, and benefit consumers, provided that clear mechanisms are established to measure such impacts while ensuring that market competition is preserved. The article concludes by pointing out growth trends in circular-economy-related operations and CADE’s essential role in regulating these practices, reinforcing the integration between economic and environmental objectives. The contribution, thus, lies in connecting the broader sustainability debate with concrete analytical tools that may strengthen both enforcement and policy in Brazil.

title: Institutional Transferability of Export Finance for Innovative Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
summary: This review examines the institutional transferability of export-financing mechanisms for innovative small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across different economic and regulatory environments. It synthesises 55 studies published between 2000 and 2025, conducts a detailed audit of 13 evidence-rich sources, identifies four finance-to-export pathways, and develops an Institutional Transferability Score (ITS) to assess the feasibility of adapting financial instruments across institutional contexts. The analysis examines venture capital, public research and development support, bank credit, export credit and insurance, trade finance, FinTech, crowdfunding, and complementary business support mechanisms. The study distinguishes direct evidence of export outcomes from findings concerning intermediate mechanisms, including innovation, investment, financing access, institutional quality, and firm capabilities. The Institutional Transferability Score evaluates eight financing configurations across five dimensions: regulatory portability, market infrastructure, digital and data feasibility, firm absorptive readiness, and public substitutability. Contextual indicators from the 2024 World Bank Enterprise Surveys for Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan complement the assessment. The findings indicate that the effectiveness and transferability of financing arrangements depend on institutional compatibility and the availability of complementary capabilities rather than the formal replication of financial instruments alone. The study offers a transparent analytical framework for evaluating and adapting export-financing mechanisms in emerging economies, with particular attention to Central Asia. This open-access deposit includes the full research manuscript and supplementary materials documenting the review protocol, evidence coding, quantitative results, transferability assessment, and sensitivity analyses.

title: The AI-Hard Disk Paradigm: Websites as Verifiable Memory for the User's Own AI
summary: This paper proposes the AI-Hard Disk paradigm, an architecture for the Internet in which a website's primary role shifts from organising human attention to supplying external artificial-intelligence agents with structured, attributable and verifiable information. The website becomes a persistent, governed memory layer; the user's chosen AI becomes the adaptive interface through which that memory is interrogated, explained and challenged. The site is an envelope around evidence: it acquires source material, curates and normalises it, computes defined measures, records how every value was obtained and exposes the result to authorised agents. Access is governed through Liquid Data Accessibility, a policy framework in which visibility is a property of resources and operations rather than of the whole site. Cryptographic fingerprints and blockchain timestamps provide independently checkable evidence of document integrity and historical existence; provenance records and deterministic calculation pipelines support semantic and computational verification. Two improvement loops reinforce each other: AI agents curate and audit the data upstream, while the user's AI explains it downstream; as models improve, both the quality of the evidence and the quality of its explanation can improve, without erasing the historical record. Financial reporting is the principal case study because heterogeneous taxonomies, accounting conventions and disclosure dates expose the limits of language-only interpretation. Mastering Financial Markets (MFM), a free observatory of the official accounts of more than ten thousand listed companies, is presented as a working implementation. The paper separates demonstrated properties from proposals and states the boundaries of each claim: cryptographic integrity does not establish factual truth, delegated interpretation does not remove legal responsibility, and automated error detection does not justify unrestricted modification of authoritative records.

title: Fishery Value Chains and Environmental Pollution in West Africa: Does Institutional Quality Matter?
summary: ABSTRACT This study analyzes the effect of integration into global value chains on environmental pollution in West Africa, specifically in the fisheries sector. It covers 13 West African countries over the period from 1990 to 2019, employing the Driscoll and Kraay estimation technique with country and year fixed effects to control for unobserved heterogeneity and cross‐sectional dependence. The results show that participating in global value chains in the fisheries sector generally helps to reduce environmental impact. The role of institutions is important: when they function well, they limit pollution, but can also, in some cases, exacerbate certain negative effects related to fishing. Based on the results, the study recommends strengthening environmental governance and protecting fisheries resources.

title: Prioritizing and selecting the G-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry using a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach: BWM-TRUST
summary: Purpose: In today's turbulent and uncertain environment, organizations are compelled to revise traditional supply chain approaches and adopt strategies that simultaneously address environmental sustainability and resilience to disruptions. Accordingly, this study aims to develop a decision-making framework for evaluating and selecting green-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry—suppliers that demonstrate both strong environmental performance and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to disruptions. Methodology: This research employs a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework that integrates the Best-Worst Method (BWM) to determine the weights of evaluation criteria with the mulTi-noRmalization mUltiDistance aSsessmenT (TRUST) technique to rank suppliers as alternatives. The evaluation criteria, categorized into "green" and "resilience" dimensions, were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert input. These criteria include: waste generation, employee training, possession of eco-friendly certifications, pollution control initiatives, responsiveness, coordination, agility, information sharing, and efficient resource utilization. Data related to five real suppliers in the natural stone industry were collected through expert surveys and fed into the proposed evaluation model. Findings: The results revealed that "efficient resource utilization" holds the highest weight among the green and resilience criteria. Furthermore, based on the TRUST-based ranking, supplier A2 was identified as the top-performing green-resilient supplier. Originality/Value: The proposed model offers a practical, structured tool to help supply chain managers enhance sustainability and resilience amid growing environmental and operational disruptions.

title: Does Supply Chain Digitalization Buffer the Impact of Geopolitical Risk on Firm Performance? Evidence from Manufacturing Firms in Emerging Asian Economies
summary: The impact of geopolitical risk on the performance of manufacturing companies in emerging Asian economies was analyzed with the mediation of resilience of supply chains and the moderation of digitalization of these chains. The proposed model was validated using the survey data collected from around 500 managers from Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Indonesia. The results revealed that geopolitical risk significantly has an adverse effect on firm performance and supply chain resilience, while resilience has an effect that is beneficial to firm performance. The geopolitical risk–performance relationship was greatly mediated by supply chain resilience. Additionally, higher the digitalization in the supply chain, the smaller was the impact of geopolitical risk on resilience, suggesting that the more resilient firms were, the lower was the impact of geopolitical risk. This study builds on knowledge on geopolitical risks and digital supply chain literature and combines two areas of research: information-processing and dynamic capability.

summary: The article examines the role and place of digital accounting in the system of information and analytical support for enterprise management under conditions of accelerated digital transformation of the business environment. A comparative characterization of traditional and digital accounting models is provided according to the speed of information processing, level of automation, analytical capacity, data storage, integration with other information systems and major risks. The functional elements of digital accounting are systematized according to operational, tactical and strategic management levels. The main problems of accounting digital transformation are identified, including technological infrastructure limitations, a shortage of digital competencies among accounting personnel, cybersecurity risks, regulatory constraints, significant initial implementation costs and fragmented digitalization. Strategic directions for the development of digital accounting are substantiated, including integration of accounting systems with ERP, CRM and other digital platforms, development of accountants’ analytical competencies, improvement of data quality control, application of artificial intelligence tools and strengthening of information security. A logical and functional approach to transforming primary accounting data into information for management decision-making is proposed, including feedback on management information needs. It is substantiated that the effectiveness of digital accounting depends not only on the level of technological support but also on the consistency of organizational, methodological, personnel and control components within a unified digital information environment of the enterprise.

title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
summary: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. Human capital and organizational learning played a central role in sustaining and institutionalizing the strategic pivot. Conclusion: Strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group represents a multidimensional organizational response to environmental uncertainty rather than an isolated managerial decision. Successful pivots require alignment among market responses, structural transformation, technological innovation, operational resilience, and organizational learning. The proposed conceptual model can help managers recognize environmental signals, coordinate adaptive actions, and strengthen organizational resilience and long-term competitiveness.

summary: The article examines the theoretical and applied principles of financial, accounting, analytical and digital support for operational management of intellectual capital of organizations in the context of digital transformation of the economy. The relevance of the study is due to the growing role of intellectual capital as a strategic resource that determines the competitiveness, innovative development, economic security and long-term sustainability of organizations. It is substantiated that traditional approaches to accounting do not provide a complete reflection of human, structural and relational capital, which limits the possibilities of their effective management and making informed management decisions. The purpose of the article is to develop theoretical and methodological provisions and practical recommendations for the formation of tools for financial, accounting, analytical and digital support for operational management of intellectual capital of organizations. In the research process, systemic, process, structural-functional, logical and comparative methods were used, as well as methods of generalization, analysis and synthesis of scientific approaches to intellectual capital management. The features of operational management of intellectual capital are identified, which consist in the continuous development of knowledge, accumulation of competencies, integration of digital technologies and the need for operational information support of management processes. An organizational and economic mechanism for operational management of intellectual capital is proposed, which is based on the interaction of financial support, accounting and analytical system, digital infrastructure, mechanisms for assessing and monitoring the effectiveness of the use of intellectual resources. A conceptual model of information support for intellectual capital management is developed, which contributes to increasing the efficiency of the use of intangible assets, optimizing management processes, accelerating digital transformation and strengthening the competitive advantages of organizations.

title: Green digital transformation and clean energy management in fashion companies: Circular economy and green innovation as pathways to sustainable performance
summary: The purpose of the present study is to analyze the capacity of green digital transformation and clean energy management to achieve sustainable performance in textile and fashion firms, considering circular economy and green innovation. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the resource-based view, the study argues that green capabilities do not automatically improve sustainable performance; rather, they require internal organizational mechanisms that make them tangible. Based on a survey administered to 283 business managers in Colombia, the proposed theoretical relationships were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that green digital transformation capability and clean energy readiness were positively associated with circular economy practices and green innovation capability, which were, in turn, positively associated with sustainable performance. The study identifies two internal organizational pathways consistent with corporate sustainability in a resource-intensive industry.

summary: The article examines reserves for improving the efficiency of human resource utilization in enterprises within the corporate governance system under martial law conditions. It is substantiated that contemporary crisis challenges necessitate the transformation of human resource management approaches and the active identification and use of internal reserves to enhance workforce performance. The study identifies key directions for improvement, including the development of employees’ adaptability and multifunctionality, digitalization of HR management processes, enhancement of motivation mechanisms, optimization of organizational structures and corporate governance systems, as well as the preservation and development of human capital. The research demonstrates that the integrated implementation of these reserves contributes to increasing organizational flexibility, improving the quality and speed of managerial decision-making, raising labor productivity, and strengthening the stability of human resource potential. Particular attention is given to the role of digital technologies, flexible organizational forms, project-based management approaches, and modern motivational tools in ensuring business continuity and operational resilience in conditions of uncertainty and disruption caused by war. It is concluded that the systematic utilization of the identified reserves within corporate governance frameworks creates prerequisites for the long-term sustainable development of enterprises, strengthens their competitive advantages, and supports the formation of resilient human capital as a key strategic resource. In addition, the implementation of these measures contributes to the adaptability of enterprises in crisis conditions and lays the foundation for effective post-war economic recovery and modernization.

title: Green Finance Policy and Firm Productivity in the Green Transition: Evidence from China’s Pilot Zones
summary: Green finance has become an important policy instrument for promoting sustainable development, but its effects on firm productivity may vary across firms with different environmental attributes. This study develops a theoretical framework in which green finance incorporates environmental performance into credit allocation and capital pricing, thereby reshaping firms’ financing conditions, innovation incentives, and resource allocation efficiency. The framework suggests that green finance may create productivity-enhancing incentives for green firms while imposing transition-related pressures on heavily polluting firms. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2024, this study exploits China’s Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones policy as a quasi-natural experiment and combines a triple-difference (DDD) model with a Double Machine Learning (DDML) framework to identify the policy’s productivity effects. The results show that the policy significantly increases the total factor productivity of green firms but reduces that of heavily polluting firms. Mechanism analysis indicates that the policy reduces both green technological innovation and capital allocation efficiency among heavily polluting firms. For green firms, the policy promotes green technological innovation but reduces capital allocation efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects vary with government subsidies, organizational slack, and industry asset intensity. Further analysis suggests that digital transformation may mitigate the policy’s adverse productivity effect on heavily polluting firms, while the policy improves governance among green firms by reducing earnings management and controlling-shareholder expropriation. These findings suggest that green finance policy should balance environmental constraints with support for firms’ green transition, adopt differentiated policy designs, and strengthen governance mechanisms to promote sustainable productivity growth and an inclusive green transition.

summary: The article explores the essence and role of economic control as a key component of an organization’s management system. It is substantiated that, under modern economic conditions, economic control is transforming from a traditional function of monitoring and detecting deviations into a proactive management tool aimed at ensuring financial stability, improving resource efficiency, minimizing risks, and achieving strategic objectives. The study emphasizes that effective economic control provides a reliable informational and analytical basis for managerial decision-making and enhances the overall adaptability of organizations to dynamic and uncertain external environments. The main policy directions of economic control are identified and systematized, including: financial stability and solvency policy, efficient use of resources policy, risk management and economic security policy, performance and productivity policy, as well as transparency and compliance policy. Each of these directions is implemented through a set of specific instruments that together form an integrated control mechanism within the management system. The content and functional purpose of key economic control tools are examined, including financial analysis, cash flow control, budgeting, cost standardization, risk analysis, internal and external audit, key performance indicators (KPIs), management accounting, and internal regulations and standards. It is demonstrated that the integrated application of these instruments ensures higher efficiency and consistency of managerial decisions, strengthens financial discipline, increases transparency of business processes, and supports sustainable organizational development. The findings confirm that an effective economic control system plays a decisive role in enhancing the competitiveness, financial resilience, and long-term growth of an organization. The study also highlights the importance of further development of economic control tools in the context of digitalization and increasing uncertainty, particularly regarding their integration into strategic management and corporate governance practices.

title: External Environmental Audits and Supply‐Chain Carbon Monitoring: Cross‐Country Evidence on Corporate Environmental Accountability
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines external energy audits and reported supply‐chain carbon monitoring using 12,154 energy‐monitoring establishments in 37 countries from the 2019‐coded World Bank Enterprise Survey cross‐section. Audit is associated with an 8.1‐percentage‐point higher monitoring probability after establishment, governance, country, and industry controls. The questionnaire limits monitoring to the chain up to establishment output; it does not measure complete Scope 3 accounting or emissions reduction. Positive associations persist under alternative estimators and wild‐cluster inference. Customer requirements, environmental managers, and strategy strengthen the association under false‐discovery and family‐wise corrections. Practice‐index associations remain positive after excluding energy‐management content that may overlap with audit. The decomposition is consistent with the proposed monitoring pathway, while cross‐sectional timing and instrument strength warrant an associational interpretation. These findings clarify how external assessment relates to value‐chain information collection and reported environmental practices.
