title: TIEROE: A Multidimensional Governance Framework for Inclusive Radio Frequency Spectrum Assignment in Developing Economies
summary: Radio frequency (RF) spectrum has emerged as a strategic public resource underpinning digital transformation, broadband connectivity, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, cloud computing, and next-generation wireless communications. As governments increasingly pursue digital economy objectives, spectrum governance has evolved from a purely technical regulatory function into a critical policy instrument shaping innovation, competition, economic development, and digital inclusion. Despite the widespread adoption of auction-based spectrum assignment mechanisms, concerns persist regarding their ability to balance economic efficiency with broader public-interest objectives, particularly within developing economies characterized by persistent digital inequalities and unequal market participation. The existing spectrum governance literature remains fragmented across technology adoption, resource capability, digital inclusion, and regulatory perspectives, providing limited guidance on how regulators can simultaneously promote efficiency, affordability, competition, equity, and universal connectivity. This study develops the Technology–Inclusion–Equity–Resource Capability–Organisation–Environment (TIEROE) framework. The TIEROE framework serves as a conceptual governance model and diagnostic tool intended to assist policymakers and regulators in the design, evaluation, and comparison of spectrum assignment mechanisms across multiple dimensions. A qualitative research design was adopted, incorporating a systematic literature review, analysis of policy and regulatory documents, and an international comparative assessment of spectrum governance practices. The findings reveal that effective spectrum governance is shaped by six interdependent dimensions: technology, inclusion, equity, resource capability, organisation, and environment. These dimensions collectively influence the extent to which spectrum assignment contributes to digital transformation and sustainable development outcomes. The study contributes to spectrum governance research by integrating previously fragmented theoretical perspectives into a unified framework. It provides policymakers with a practical governance tool for designing inclusive spectrum assignment mechanisms. The TIEROE framework extends existing technology adoption and digital inclusion theories and offers a foundation for future empirical research on spectrum governance within developing economies.

title: Challenging assumptions in supply chain management accounting and reporting: a metamodern sustainability transformation
summary: Purpose This paper aims to use a metamodern approach and a problematization lens to challenge the assumption that transparency driven accounting of historical social and environmental harms is sufficient to achieve the scale of sustainability transformation of supply chains required by scientific evidence. It argues that sustainability measurement, accounting and reporting must also encompass future orientated, positive and absolute sustainability contributions enabled by transformative product, business model and supply chain redesign. Design/methodology/approach A metamodern approach is introduced and used in the paper. Drawing on metamodernism, the paper develops a framework for oscillating between incremental, transparency-based measurement and more fundamental assessments of business development. Through problematization of existing literature, it identifies limiting assumptions and advances accounting and reporting for sustainable supply chain transformations. Findings The analysis reveals four dominant assumptions in sustainability accounting and reporting that constrain sufficiently far-reaching sustainability transformations of supply chains: backward looking transparency, supplier assessment logics, harm reduction framing and incremental improvements. The proposed metamodern framework broadens the role of accounting by integrating multiple intelligence sources to support monitoring of existing supply chains and identification of redesign opportunities aligned with planetary boundaries and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Research limitations/implications The paper provides a metamodern foundation for future empirical development and testing of transformative sustainability measurement and accounting that embraces different intelligence sources. Practical implications Measurement and accounting informed by metamodern theory oscillates between different intelligence sources, comprising data, information and knowledge, to support both monitoring of existing supply chain relationships and identification of transformative redesign opportunities. Social implications The argument supports development of supply chain strategies and designs capable of addressing the easing of social and environmental harms as well as development of transformative sustainability opportunities. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first paper to apply a metamodern lens to sustainability accounting and reporting for supply chain management. It shows how oscillation between modernist and postmodern logics opens new pathways for theorizing transformative measurement and positions accounting information as a catalyst for strategic redesign rather than incremental optimization.

title: Paradigma Shallow Ecology dan Deep Ecology dalam Kebijakan Hukum Lingkungan: Analisis Kerusakan Mangrove di Teluk Benoa
summary: Environmental degradation has become a critical issue in modern legal discourse, particularly in relation to natural resource management and sustainable development policies. The damage to mangrove ecosystems in Benoa Bay, Bali, allegedly caused by hydrocarbon contamination from energy distribution activities, illustrates the conflict between economic development interests and environmental protection. In the context of legal philosophy, this phenomenon reflects the dominance of the shallow ecology paradigm, which views nature primarily as an instrument for human economic interests, rather than the deep ecology paradigm that recognizes the intrinsic value of nature and the interconnectedness between humans and ecosystems. Previous studies have generally examined mangrove ecosystem degradation from ecological, environmental management, or policy implementation perspectives. However, limited attention has been given to philosophical analysis regarding how legal paradigms influence environmental policy and environmental governance. This study aims to analyze how the paradigms of shallow ecology and deep ecology influence environmental legal policies and how these paradigms can explain the occurrence of mangrove ecosystem degradation in Benoa Bay. This research uses a normative juridical method with a philosophical and conceptual approach. The locus of the study focuses on the mangrove ecosystem in Benoa Bay as a case study of environmental degradation. Data were obtained through literature studies of legal regulations, environmental law doctrines, scientific publications, and previous research findings. The analysis was conducted through qualitative and normative interpretation by examining legal principles related to environmental protection, particularly those contained in Law Number 32 of 2009 concerning Environmental Protection and Management. The findings indicate that environmental policies that prioritize economic growth tend to reflect the shallow ecology paradigm, which potentially weakens environmental protection mechanisms. The novelty of this research lies in its philosophical analysis of environmental law by emphasizing the importance of integrating the deep ecology paradigm into environmental policy-making and legal enforcement. The study recommends strengthening environmental governance, enhancing supervision of environmental permits and environmental impact assessments, and incorporating ecological justice principles into environmental law policies. Future research is encouraged to develop interdisciplinary approaches that integrate environmental philosophy, environmental law, and sustainable development frameworks

title: Interside: Blockchain Interoperability Architecture for Supply Chain Tracking
summary: Modern supply chains rely on permissioned blockchain networks that frequently operate as isolated entities, resulting in fragmented data, limited visibility, and inconsistent governance. This research addresses these challenges by proposing “Interside,” an interoperability framework designed explicitly for multi-network supply chain ecosystems. Using a design science research methodology, the study includes requirement analysis, framework development, prototype implementation, and a preliminary evaluation. The architecture features a main-chain/side-chain model that preserves network autonomy while enabling secure, auditable cross-chain communication and selective data sharing via a dedicated side-chain tracking ledger. A prototype was built with Hyperledger Fabric and Weaver components, and the framework was evaluated through a conceptual comparison with direct and hub-based approaches. Results show that Interside improves decentralization, governance autonomy, and auditability compared with existing models, with minor trade-offs in prototype performance. This work introduces a novel architectural blueprint for permissioned blockchain interoperability in supply chain environments and outlines practical directions for future large-scale performance benchmarking.

title: Strategic decisions on blockchain adoption and fee structure in a heterogeneous consumer market
summary: This study investigates a supply chain with a manufacturer and a retailer, where the manufacturer faces the decision of when and how to introduce blockchain in collaboration with a blockchain service firm to serve heterogeneous consumers. The blockchain service firm and the manufacturer negotiate under three alternative fee structures to determine the specific fee offered by the manufacturer. Through the comparison of equilibrium results in the presence and absence of blockchain adoption, we illustrate that the decisions of whether and with which fee structure to adopt blockchain are principally contingent on the trade-off between the benefits arising from market expansion and the costs of blockchain, which are driven by the interplay among the consumers’ average traceability awareness, the fraction of information-sensitive consumers, and the blockchain service firm’s fixed cost. Moreover, our analysis also demonstrates that the manufacturer will solely choose the annual lump-sum fee or unit usage fee to cooperate with the blockchain service firm, while the mixed fee will never be chosen. Additionally, the annual lump-sum fee emerges as the only viable option to ensure profitable outcomes for all members. Notably, we consider two extensions: mixed cost borne by the blockchain service firm and stochastic demand. The extended analyses reveal that the mixed fee may become the optimal choice under specific conditions when the blockchain service firm bears mixed cost. Meanwhile, the main outcomes remain robust under stochastic demand. Overall, these findings provide valuable managerial insights for firms evaluating blockchain adoption and designing effective fee structures in heterogeneous consumer markets. This study explores the adoption decisions within the framework of a triadic supply chain, involving the manufacturer, retailer, and the blockchain service firm. This expanded analytical framework reveals that the feasibility of blockchain adoption not merely relies on technology costs but depends more on the interaction of market structure, consumer heterogeneity, and inter-firm power dynamics. The insights from our analysis can provide valuable managerial guidance for firms on when and how to introduce blockchain by cooperating with blockchain service firms.

title: ЦИФРОВА ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ МЕХАНІЗМІВ СТРАТЕГІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ ФІНАНСОВОЮ СИСТЕМОЮ ДЕРЖАВИ: ПОТЕНЦІАЛ, ОБМЕЖЕННЯ ТА НАПРЯМИ ВПРОВАДЖЕННЯ
summary: The object of the research is the strategic management mechanisms of the state financial system under digital transformation. One of the main problems is the identification of digital transformation with the volume of technology adoption, so that resources go to automating processes that are not the management bottleneck. The purpose of the study is to determine the potential and the limits of the digital transformation of strategic management mechanisms and to substantiate the directions of its implementation in Ukraine. The information base consists of the Strategy of the financial sector development of Ukraine, the European Union acts on digital operational resilience, materials of the Bank for International Settlements and papers in peer-reviewed journals. The systemic approach, comparative analysis of strategic documents, typologisation and structural functional analysis were applied. It is established that digital tasks are present in two of the five strategic goals of the national strategy, yet they are detailed only for service development and the internal efficiency of regulators and are almost absent for interagency coordination. A criterion is proposed for distinguishing managerial deficits by their nature: digital means resolve problems of informational and coordinative origin but not those of political, institutional or structural origin. Under this criterion, three of the five systemic problems of strategic management in Ukraine are amenable to a digital solution: fragmented goal setting, weak interagency coordination and regulatory asymmetry. A five-step implementation sequence is substantiated, each step relying on the previous one. The originality lies in substantiating a criterion that matches a digital instrument with the deficit it addresses, instead of assessment by the volume of technology adoption. The proposed distinction can be applied when shaping digitalisation programmes of financial regulators to prioritise expenditure.

title: The Impact of Local Government Green Attention on Firms’ New Quality Productive Forces: Evidence from China’s A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Drawing on a panel of 31,025 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share listed companies over 2010–2024, this study examines the relationship between local government green attention (GreenAtt) and corporate new quality productive forces (NQPF). GreenAtt is derived from prefecture-level government work reports, while corporate NQPF is measured using a multidimensional composite index. In the fully specified fixed-effects model, the estimated coefficient on GreenAtt is 0.000150 and is statistically significant at the 5% level. A one-standard-deviation increase in GreenAtt is associated with an estimated increase of approximately 0.004 in NQPF, equivalent to about 3.5% of the dependent variable’s sample standard deviation. This finding remains robust across multiple robustness checks and alternative model specifications. Further mechanism-related regressions show a negative association between GreenAtt and financing constraints and a positive association between GreenAtt and green innovation, consistent with the proposed mechanisms. Environmental regulation also moderates this relationship, with the interaction between GreenAtt and environmental regulation exhibiting a positive and statistically significant coefficient. When environmental regulation is one standard deviation above its sample mean, the estimated marginal effect of GreenAtt is approximately 31.2% greater than its value at the mean level of regulation. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that the positive relationship is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms outside heavily polluting industries, and firms located in resource-based cities. Overall, these findings provide firm-level evidence linking local governments’ green policy priorities to corporate productive upgrading and highlight differences across institutional and industrial contexts.

title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
summary: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

title: A Quantitative Framework for Assessing Digital Sovereignty
summary: Digital sovereignty is a political buzzword. However, there are diverging views on how to define and measure it. Throughout this study we propose the creation of a quantitative framework to measure digital sovereignty capabilities on a country's performance in three key areas: technology, government, and users. Through our analysis covering 123 countries, we have shown the different paths towards achieving sovereignty that are imprinted into how the countries contribute to the digital economy and reflect the asymmetries existing in the global value chains. The US and China both show a strong technological leadership, especially regarding emerging technologies, while the EU maintains a balance between innovation and regulations that the new strategies and MFF must address in order to become a relevant global player.

title: Legal Safeguards for Food Security in the Context of ESG Transformation in the Agricultural Sector
summary: The article provides a comprehensive scientific and legal analysis of the legal guarantees of food security in Ukraine under the conditions of ESG transformation of the agricultural sector through the prism of modern agricultural law doctrine. It is substantiated that, in the context of martial law, global climate change, and European integration, food security acquires the character of a complex interdisciplinary legal category combining constitutional guarantees of the human right to adequate food with the principles of sustainable agricultural development. Within the system of agricultural law, food security is defined as an independent direction of legal regulation related to the rational use of agricultural land, stability of agricultural production, and proper functioning of agri-food markets. The article analyzes the regulatory framework for ensuring food security, including the provisions of the Constitution of Ukraine, land and environmental legislation, legal acts on environmental impact assessment, anti-corruption regulation and corporate governance, as well as relevant international legal instruments and approaches developed by FAO, OECD, and the EU acquis in the field of sustainable development. Particular attention is paid to the role of implementing European standards of non-financial reporting and sustainable finance in modernizing agricultural legal regulation. The environmental, social, and governance components of legal guarantees of food security are examined as structural elements of the agricultural legal mechanism. The environmental dimension covers the protection of land and water resources, preservation of soil fertility, and climate change adaptation; the social dimension includes guarantees of decent working conditions, support for small and medium-sized producers, and ensuring food accessibility; the governance dimension encompasses transparency, accountability, and proper corporate control in the agricultural sector. It is concluded that the integration of ESG principles transforms both the subject matter and the method of agricultural law, forming a new model of legal guarantees of food security as a multi-level system of norms, principles, and institutions. The necessity of further development of agricultural law doctrine and harmonization of Ukrainian legislation with European approaches is substantiated in order to ensure the resilience of Ukraine’s agri-food system in the face of military, economic, and climate challenges. The methodological framework of the article is based on a combination of general scientific and special legal methods, including the dialectical, systemic, formal-legal, and comparative-legal approaches. The systemic method made it possible to examine food security as a multidimensional legal category within the context of ESG transformation of the agricultural sector. The formal-legal analysis was applied to study national legislation, including the Constitution of Ukraine, relevant UN instruments, and documents of FAO and OECD, as well as the EU acquis. The comparative-legal method and legal forecasting were used to substantiate directions for harmonizing Ukrainian legislation with sustainable development principles and ESG standards.

title: A Study on The Evolving Financial Landscape, Risk Dynamics and Institutional Integration of Cryptocurrency in India
summary: Abstract The rapid development of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology has significantly influenced the global financial landscape, creating new opportunities for digital financial innovation while introducing various financial, technological, and regulatory challenges. This study examines the evolving financial landscape of cryptocurrency in India, with particular emphasis on risk dynamics and institutional integration. It explores the development of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), the major risks associated with cryptocurrency, and the regulatory mechanisms introduced by the Government of India and financial authorities. The study focuses on market volatility, cybersecurity threats, consumer protection, money laundering, financial stability, taxation, and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) compliance. It also examines the growing relationship between cryptocurrency-related activities, financial institutions, fintech organisations, and India's broader digital-finance ecosystem. The research adopts a secondary and descriptive analytical approach based on publications from the Reserve Bank of India, the Income Tax Department, the Financial Intelligence Unit–India, the Bank for International Settlements, and other credible sources. The study highlights the importance of balancing technological innovation with effective regulation, risk management, and consumer protection. It concludes that a transparent and well-structured regulatory framework is essential for addressing cryptocurrency-related risks and supporting the responsible development of India's digital financial ecosystem.

title: Staff ICT Training as the Binding Constraint on Accrual-Based IPSAS in Zimbabwean Government Schools: A case of Marondera District
summary: ABSTRACT: Implementing Accrual-based International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) require ICT skills from schools accounting personnel. Unfortunately, training for this new era has not been given priority in Zimbabwe. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the extent to which staff ICT training would influence accrual based IPSAS implementation within government schools in Marondera District. A convergent mixed-methods case study surveyed 71 school heads, bursars, accounts and administrative staff and Ministry officials. The response rate was 97.3%. Ten key informants were interviewed. Interviews were analysed thematically. Staff ICT training was the weakest of six digital transformation constructs (M = 2.16). None of its five items differed significantly from neutral (p = 0.139– 0.728), and responses were split almost evenly, with 46.8% agreeing and 43.4% disagreeing. The lowest-rated implementation item was staff ability to recognise revenues and expenses when incurred (M = 2.44). Interviewees described training as periodic, generic workshops rather than role-specific capacity building. Training, not attitudes to technology, was the binding human constraint. Structured, practical and recurrent IPSAS and software training for school finance staff was recommended. KEYWORDS: Accrual based accounting; IPSAS; ICT training; Technology acceptance; Government schools. title: Exploring Autonomous Vehicle Adoption in Logistics Small- and Medium-Sized Enterprises: A Framework for Emerging Economies
summary: Autonomous vehicle (AV) technologies are increasingly viewed as strategic enablers of digital transformation in logistics, yet existing adoption frameworks only partially explain organisational readiness among logistics small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. This study develops the Process–Organisation–Environment–Technology (POET) framework as an integrated conceptual explanation of AV adoption readiness in logistics SMEs. Using a conceptual theory-building approach, the study synthesises the literature on technology adoption, organisational readiness, socio-technical systems, digital transformation, logistics SME operations, and AV adoption, with contextual grounding drawn from the South African logistics SME setting. The POET framework conceptualises AV adoption readiness as a multidimensional organisational capability emerging from the alignment of process integration, organisational readiness, environmental readiness, and technological maturity. The study contributes to organisational technology adoption theory by positioning process capability as an explicit analytical dimension alongside organisational, environmental, and technological readiness, offering a context-sensitive framework for understanding AV adoption readiness in infrastructure-constrained logistics SMEs. The framework provides a theoretical foundation for future empirical operationalisation and supports managers and policymakers in identifying capability, process, technological, and environmental conditions that may enable sustainable digital transformation.

title: Social imaginaries on wildfires, burning practices, and fire management in two Colombian national newspapers: tensions between risk, illegality, and ecological function
summary: Introduction This article analyzes the construction of social imaginaries about the application of fire in two Colombian national newspapers, El Tiempo and El Espectador , based on three key concepts understood as distinct discursive categories: fire use and management, burning practices, and wildfires. Methodology A mixed-methods approach is adopted, combining artificial intelligence tools with qualitative analysis. The quantitative phase employs a BETO model to classify the evaluative framing of fire, while the qualitative phase utilizes a discursive analysis. The corpus consists of 504 items published in El Tiempo and El Espectador between 2020 and 2025. Results The findings show that, in the coverage of both newspapers, the application of fire is primarily represented as a problematic practice, associated with risk, illegality, and destruction. This trend is quantified by the predominance of negative valuations within the corpus. Based on the automatic classification of text fragments, 71% present a negative valuation, compared to 29% neutral. Specifically, “burning practices” concentrate 87.5% negative valuations and 12.5% neutral, while “wildfires” record 68% negative and 32% neutral, with no positive valuations identified in the manually annotated sample. In contrast, “fire use and management” has marginal visibility in the corpus, with only 24 news items; their manual classification as complete news items, reported separately because of its different unit and procedure, shows that 15 (62%) were positive and 9 (38%) negative, despite the potential of this concept to recognize ecological and territorial functions. Discussion These findings suggest that terminological distribution may contribute to consolidating interpretive frameworks that reduce the complexity of the phenomenon. Consequently, the analyzed coverage tends to leave the ecological and cultural dimensions of fire in the background, which may limit the legitimacy of integrated management approaches in environmental governance.

title: A Study of the Dual Facets of Third-Party Logistics Partnerships: Opportunities and Risks in Modern Supply Chains
summary: This paper explores the opportunities, risks, and rewards of companies outsourcing functions, specifically supply chain or logistics functions through an outside entity or a third-party provider. Today’s markets are global in nature, and to be competitive in this global market, companies have to make critical decisions, including the outsourcing of some, if not all, of their supply chain or logistics functions. Outsourcing is a decision that should be approached carefully, as its benefits might not outweigh its costs. The outsourcing proposition has to make sense in various aspects, not only cost, as companies have to balance more than one type of shareholder, as they have ESG commitments (Environmental, Social and Governance) to account for. Plus; off the heels of the recent COVID-19 pandemic, selecting a reliable third- party logistics provider (3PL) is more important than ever to navigate similar future events or other natural disasters that disrupt supply chains.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
summary: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

title: CEO facial masculinity and real earnings management: a machine learning approach
summary: Purpose Using a machine learning approach, this paper analyzes the relationship between chief executive officer (CEO) facial masculinity and real earnings management (REM) in the Asian context. Design/methodology/approach The analyses were based on a dataset of 348 listed firms from India, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Singapore from 2015 to 2024. The authors employed a machine learning framework using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model to predict REM. CEO facial masculinity was measured using the facial width-to-height ratio (fWHR), obtained from photographs of the CEOs collected from publicly available sources. To improve the interpretability of the model, SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were applied to determine the relative contribution and directional influence of CEO- and firm-level characteristics. Findings The findings indicate that the LightGBM model provides satisfactory predictive performance across the three REM channels, with the strongest performance observed for abnormal discretionary expenses (ABDISEXP). SHAP analysis reveals that CEO facial masculinity is a meaningful factor in explaining REM, while firm-level financial characteristics remain important determinants. Compared with conventional CEO demographic characteristics, such as age and tenure, fWHR demonstrates relatively stronger predictive importance in identifying income-increasing REM. Country-level SHAP results further suggest that the influence of CEO facial masculinity and other explanatory variables varies across institutional settings. Research limitations/implications This research offers valuable insights into the field of study, particularly regarding the biological characteristics of CEOs in relation to earnings management. The findings offer new evidence that CEO facial masculinity is a significant factor in earnings management and highlight the importance of integrating executive physical characteristics into the study of managerial decision-making and corporate governance. Originality/value While much of the prior literature has primarily focused on the managerial aspects of CEOs, this study focuses on their biological characteristics. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first research attempt to investigate this issue using a machine learning approach. The study provides novel evidence that behavioral traits captured through facial characteristics offer incremental explanatory power beyond traditional financial and demographic determinants of earnings management.

title: The Obstacle Factors and Optimization Path of the Operation Efficiency of Third-party Logistics Enterprises under the Background of Digital Intelligence Transformation
summary: In 2025, China’s total social logistics volume hit 368.2 trillion yuan, with the ratio of total social logistics costs to GDP dropping below 14% for the first time. While the logistics industry has achieved phased success in cost reduction and efficiency improvement, traditional cost cutting approaches yield diminishing marginal returns. Besides, industry differentiation is increasingly prominent: leading enterprises have harvested fruits from digital transformation, yet most small and medium-sized third-party logistics (3PL) enterprises remain in exploratory transformation. Taking these SMEs as the research subject, this paper identifies four core barriers hindering operational efficiency during digital and intelligent upgrading: misalignment between technology adoption and business scenarios, data silos and poor system coordination, inadequate organizational capability and talent shortage, as well as mismatched resource input and expected returns. These barriers interact with each other and create a self-reinforcing vicious cycle: inefficient investment further reduces enterprises’ willingness to invest. Accordingly, this study proposes three optimization paths, including lightweight deployment priority, scenario-driven implementation and progressive iteration. The findings can provide theoretical support for the digital transformation of small and medium-sized 3PL enterprises.

title: The Influence of Corporate Social Responsibility on Company Performance: The Moderating Role of Green Banking and Bank Health
summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effect of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) on firm performance, as well as to investigate the moderating role of green banking and bank soundness in this relationship. The study focuses on the banking sector. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data collected from annual and sustainability reports of banking institutions. The data were analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The empirical results indicate that CSR has a positive effect on firm performance. Furthermore, green banking and bank soundness significantly moderate the relationship between CSR and firm performance. These findings provide practical implications for banking management to integrate environmental practices and maintain bank soundness to enhance corporate performance and sustainable value creation.

title: THE PHILOSOPHY OF ZERO TOLERANCE AND ANTICORRUPTION: TRANSFORMATION FROM LEGAL NIHILISM TO LEGAL CULTURE AND SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY
summary: From the perspectives of philosophy of law and governance sociology, this research article analyzes the phenomenon of 'zero tolerance' as a fundamental catalyst in combating corruption. It examines the structural vector of societal consciousness shifting from deeply rooted legal nihilism toward a mature legal culture and high social responsibility. Within the IMRAD methodological framework (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), based on conceptual analysis, a representative sociological survey(N = 1,200), and institutional change modeling, this paper demonstrates that punitive state mechanisms are inefficient without altering everyday societal perceptions of corruption. A conceptual model of socio-legal transformation is formulated alongside actionable recommendations for embedding zero-tolerance principles into public governance and corporate governance frameworks

title: Provincial Data-Factor Capability and Individual Employment in China: A Multilevel Socio-Technical Systems Perspective
summary: Employment adjustment under digital transformation is a multilevel outcome that depends not only on regional technical capability but also on the structural configuration and worker response conditions in which that capability is embedded. This study examines the relationship between provincial data-factor capability and individual employment in China by matching China Family Panel Studies data for 2012–2022 with a provincial DataIndex. Binary Logit models with province and year fixed effects reveal an age gradient: the employment association of DataIndex is positive for younger workers, weakens around midlife, and becomes negative at older ages. Province-year regressions further show that stronger data-factor capability is associated with industrial structure upgrading and greater regional innovation activity, while interaction tests indicate less favorable employment associations among agricultural-hukou and rural residents. These findings show that improvements in regional digital capability do not translate uniformly into employment gains. Instead, their labor-market consequences depend on worker adaptability and institutional and spatial conditions. The study therefore highlights the need to evaluate digital transformation not only through technological and structural progress, but also through the inclusiveness of its employment outcomes.

title: Market Dominance and Competitive Effects of Online Travel Platforms: A Case Study of Ctrip/Trip.com Group in China
summary: The rapid expansion of China’s digital economy has made online travel agencies (OTAs) an important intermediary between consumers and suppliers of accommodation, transport and tourism services. At the same time, platform concentration, network effects and contractual restrictions can create substantial market power. This study examines Ctrip and its parent, Trip.com Group, as a case through which to evaluate the formation and competitive effects of platform dominance. The analysis combines publicly available industry and corporate data with a June 2026 consumer questionnaire. It also incorporates a factual update based on the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) decision of July 2026. The revised analysis finds strong evidence that Trip.com Group has substantial market power, particularly in online hotel-booking platform services, but it avoids treating broad OTA gross merchandise value (GMV) shares as a legally sufficient measure of dominance. The platform’s scale can generate efficiencies through matching, standardisation, service quality and investment in digital infrastructure; however, dominance may also facilitate exclusionary contracting and restrictions on hotel pricing. The consumer survey suggests high brand salience and potential switching behaviour, but its non-probability sample and several instrument inconsistencies prevent causal or population-level inference. Overall, the evidence supports a balanced view: platform scale can improve coordination and consumer convenience, while competition policy remains necessary where contractual or algorithmic mechanisms restrict merchant autonomy or foreclose rivals.

title: Digital economy and integrated pollution–carbon pressure: spatial spillovers and evidence from Chinese cities
summary: Digital transformation is increasingly recognized as an important pathway toward urban sustainability. However, how digital economy development affects integrated pollution–carbon pressure across spatially connected cities remains insufficiently understood. Using a balanced panel dataset of 266 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2010 to 2023, this study constructs an integrated pollution–carbon pressure index (IPCB) and employs a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Model to examine the environmental effects of digital economy development. The results show that digital economy development is significantly associated with lower IPCB, indicating that digital transformation contributes to alleviating the combined environmental pressure generated by conventional pollutants and carbon emissions. Spatial-effect decomposition further reveals significant negative direct, indirect, and total effects, suggesting that the environmental benefits of digitalization extend beyond local administrative boundaries through spatial spillovers. Exploratory subgroup analyses reveal differing coefficient patterns across regions, urban-agglomeration status, and city-size groups; because formal cross-group coefficient-equality tests are not conducted, these patterns are interpreted as exploratory rather than as statistically confirmed heterogeneity. Moreover, energy consumption intensity and artificial intelligence attention strengthen the negative association between digital economy development and IPCB, highlighting the importance of local conditions in translating digital transformation into environmental improvements. The main negative association is supported by alternative measurement and permutation-based placebo tests, while the sample-exclusion, lagged-variable, and policy-based checks reveal some variation in local and spillover estimates. These results emphasize the role of digital connectivity, targeted digital upgrading, and technology-related information diffusion in supporting sustainable urban development.

title: The Impact of Female Directors on Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from China
summary: Green innovation has become an important driving force for enterprises to shape competitive advantages and for countries to restructure the industrial competitive landscape, but existing research has not reached a consistent conclusion on whether and how female directors affect corporate green innovation. Based on data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2023, this study empirically examines the impact of female directors on corporate green innovation. The results show that female directors can significantly improve the level of corporate green innovation, and this conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests. The mechanism analysis indicates that female directors promote green innovation by improving corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. The heterogeneity analysis finds that this effect is more significant in non-state-owned enterprises, industries with low competition, and young enterprises. From the perspective of board gender composition, this study reveals the internal mechanism through which female directors affect corporate green innovation and provides empirical evidence for understanding the economic consequences of board gender diversity and for enterprises seeking to improve their green innovation level.

title: The Institutionalization of REIT Sustainability Reporting: Cross‐Country Evidence From ESG Disclosure Regimes and Building Sustainability Policies
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the institutionalization and textual evolution of sustainability reporting among listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, and Japan between 2020 and 2025. Reporting is framed as the joint product of two institutional layers: capital‐market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure regimes and building‐level sustainability policies. For the full listed universe (641 REIT‐year observations), the analysis combines transition modeling with binomial logit estimation. To analyze the text of 307 hand‐collected reports, it applies term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF–IDF) comparison, Structural Topic Modeling, and a human‐validated building‐level sustainability keyword index. The share of listed REITs issuing an identifiable sustainability report rose from 43.1% to 63.9%; new adoption (26.4%) far outpaced discontinuation (5.1%). Reporting language shifted toward structured, climate‐oriented, and implementation‐focused content. Asset‐level sustainability vocabulary is densest where building‐level instruments are longest established and rose fastest where those instruments expanded. The two layers leave distinguishable traces: disclosure regimes most visibly on the issuance margin, building policies on the content margin. The proposed index offers a transferable starting point for monitoring asset‐level sustainability language in corporate disclosure.

title: Securing the Robotics Supply Chain
summary: This paper sets out what a sustained federal research and investment agenda would need to include to close that gap--not within a single budget cycle, but over the decade such an undertaking will realistically require. It identifies where the gap is most pronounced today: in the methods needed to verify and certify components of uncertain origin, in the foundational hardware research that has long been underfunded relative to software, in the physical infrastructure researchers need to test systems at scale, and in the workforce required to build and sustain all of it. Robotics should not be treated merely as a downstream beneficiary of a broader artificial intelligence investment strategy. It constitutes its own supply chain, with its own points of failure, and merits its own sustained federal commitment.

title: INNOVATIVE APPROACHES IN MARKETING: PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND PROMOTION IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITALIZATION
summary: The modern approach to product creation is based not on intuitive ideas, but on the real-time analysis of users' digital behavior. It allows for predicting audience demands and actively shaping them by adapting the product to specific scenarios. Amid information overload, consumers place high demands on the quality and personalization of service. To build long-term relationships with the audience, brands need to ensure a seamless digital experience at all stages of interaction. The article explores modern innovative approaches to product development and promotion within the context of the economy's digital transformation. Special attention is paid to how digitalization is changing the logic of product creation and marketing communications: the focus shifts toward data, the speed of response to market demands, and the delivery of a seamless customer experience. The transformation of the product lifecycle stages is analyzed separately, covering the acceleration of time-to-market for new products through digital prototyping and split testing, dynamic positioning management based on real-time analytics, and the adaptation of promotion strategies to audience behavior on social media and marketplaces. The key tools shaping these new practices are examined, including artificial intelligence and machine learning for demand forecasting and offer adaptation, big data for segmentation and hypothesis testing, immersive technologies for audience engagement, and omnichannel systems. The research results allow for systemizing current innovative methods and offering practical recommendations for their implementation in organizations' marketing activities, taking into account the business's level of digital maturity and the specifics of the target audience. The recommendations on innovative approaches have been tested at an Omsk confectionery enterprise. The article will be of interest to corporate executives, marketers, and brand managers.

title: Corporate social responsibility inequality and persistent anemia burden: insights from KBK region of Odisha, India
summary: Background: Anemia remains a major public health concern in India, with NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 documenting increasing prevalence among women and children. Despite growing corporate social responsibility (CSR) investment, regional inequities persist, particularly in Odisha’s vulnerable KBK region. This study examines anemia trends across India, selected states, and KBK districts and assesses their alignment with CSR spending on health and nutrition. Methods: A secondary-data analysis used NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 factsheets, official government datasets and portals, and CSR disclosures. Descriptive, comparative, and trend analyses assessed anemia prevalence and the distribution of corporate investment in health, nutrition, water, and sanitation. Results: Anemia among pregnant women increased nationally, while KBK districts consistently exceeded state and national averages. Odisha’s CSR expenditure on health, hunger and malnutrition, drinking water, and sanitation rose from ₹130.58 crore in 2019 to ₹416.27 crore in 2024; however, anemia among women of reproductive age increased by 13.3% between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5. Improvements in health- and water-related SDGs contrasted with weaker poverty outcomes, suggesting that higher expenditure alone has not resolved underlying nutritional and socio-economic barriers. Conclusions: Anemia reduction in the KBK region requires better-targeted CSR investment aligned with local governance and public programmes. Priorities include stronger ICDS implementation, community-based nutrition education, reliable iron and folic acid supplementation, and improved healthcare access in vulnerable areas.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility Techniques in Wooing New Converts to The Redeemed Christian Church of God Port Harcourt
summary: The study investigated corporate social responsibility techniques employed by churches, specifically the Redeemed Christian Church of God in Port Harcourt, to woo members effectively. The objectives of the study were to: identify corporate social responsibility techniques employed by churches, specifically the Redeemed Christian Church of God in Port Harcourt, to wooing members effectively; identify the corporate social responsibility techniques employed by the Redeemed Christian Church of God in Port Harcourt in wooing members. The study was hinged on Stakeholders, Transformational Leadership, and Social Contract Theories. The study employed a survey research design with a total population of 3190 using Krejcie and Morgan sample size determination table to arrive 341. It employed stratified random sampling and used a questionnaire and a question guide as the instruments for data collection. It adopted the Weighted Mean Score on a 4-point Likert scale as the method of data analysis. The results of the study revealed that corporate social responsibility techniques were employed by Redeemed Christian Church of God in Port Harcourt in wooing members; corporate social responsibility activities address the social needs of members to the Redeemed Christian Church of God in Port Harcourt. The study recommends that The Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) should formally integrate corporate social responsibility into its evangelism framework, and The Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) leadership should develop a formal monitoring and evaluation system to assess the relevance and effectiveness of its corporate social responsibility programmes in wooing and retaining members.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE COMPLIANCE IN STATE-OWNED ENTERPRISES IN UGANDA: A CRITICAL EXAMINATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
summary: This review examines corporate governance compliance in Uganda's state-owned enterprises (SOEs), focusing on board composition and independence, internal audit and controls, transparency and disclosure, accountability, and the relationship between governance arrangements and organizational performance. Uganda's legal framework includes the Public Enterprises Reform and Divestiture Act and the Public Finance Management Act. International standards, particularly the OECD Guidelines on Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises, provide benchmarks on professional state ownership, board autonomy, disclosure, audit and accountability. Uganda-specific literature includes studies of corporate governance and internal audit in SOEs, a case study of the National Water and Sewerage Corporation (NWSC), and research on governance attributes and commercial SOE performance. Official audit material has also reported gaps in consolidation coverage and the absence of a comprehensive database of public corporations and state enterprises. The available evidence suggests that compliance is multidimensional: formal rules are necessary, but their effectiveness depends on professional boards, independent audit, reliable information and follow-through on recommendations. This is a preliminary review, not yet a completed reproducible systematic review: formal multi-database searches, independent screening, quality appraisal and final PRISMA counts must be completed before journal submission. 2. Background State-owned enterprises operate at the intersection of public policy and commercial activity. They may deliver essential services, manage strategic infrastructure, pursue commercial objectives or combine these mandates. Their governance is complex because the state acts as owner on behalf of citizens, while ministries, boards, executives, regulators, auditors and Parliament may exercise different oversight functions. The OECD (2024) observes that this chain of accountability can obscure responsibility and create incentives that do not necessarily serve the long-term interests of the enterprise or the public. Uganda's legal framework recognises both operational autonomy and accountability. The Public Enterprises Reform and Divestiture Act identifies autonomy in operational and financial management, accountability, performance improvement, clear board functions and qualified appointments as important conditions for managing public enterprises. The Public Finance Management Act defines state enterprises to include certain statutory bodies and companies controlled by government and provides a broader framework for public financial management, reporting and internal controls. The existence of rules, however, does not establish that every enterprise implements them effectively.

title: "Digital transformation in accountancy: a study of emerging technologies, adoption challenges, and future implications"
summary: Abstract The field of accountancy has undergone a paradigm shift in the last two decades due to rapid technological advancements. Traditional bookkeeping and manual ledger systems have been replaced by cloud-based accounting software, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics tools. This paper explores the integration of technology in accountancy, examining how automation, AI-driven audit tools, cloud ERP systems, and blockchain are redefining accounting practices. It further analyses the benefits such as enhanced accuracy, real-time reporting, fraud detection, and cost efficiency, alongside challenges including cybersecurity risks, skill gaps, and resistance to change. The study employs a mixed-method approach, reviewing secondary literature and industry reports from 2020-2026 to assess technology adoption trends among small, medium, and large enterprises in India. Findings suggest that while large firms have embraced digital transformation, MSMEs lag due to cost and awareness barriers. The paper concludes that technology in accountancy is no longer optional but a strategic necessity, recommending continuous upskilling, regulatory support, and phased digital adoption for sustainable growth.
